processes.name: New-hire benefits enrollment
processes.summary: Enrolls every new hire in statutory social insurance from the first day of work and in company health, insurance and retirement plans within the local election window. Covers the US (ACA-compliant waiting period, 30-day elections, 401(k) auto-enrollment), Canada day-one group benefits, India EPF/ESI and group mediclaim, and Taiwan/China statutory enrollment plus supplemental cover. Good looks like: no coverage gaps, no late statutory registrations and correct deductions on the first payroll.
processes.owner: Benefits (process), Total Rewards (plan design), Payroll (deductions and statutory remittances)
processes.trigger: Hire transaction completed in Darwinbox (ON-03), or a rehire or move into a benefits-eligible class
outputs: Eligibility determination and benefit class in Darwinbox
Statutory registrations (BLI/NHI, social insurance/housing fund, EPF UAN/ESI) with filing receipts
Elections, dependant, beneficiary and nomination records
Carrier EDI enrollment file and ID cards
Payroll deduction and imputed-income setup
processes.sla: Statutory: Day 1 (TW), within 30 days (CN), first contribution cycle (IN); US/CA elections within 30 days of hire with coverage by the first of the month after hire

steps.label: Complete hire transaction in Darwinbox
steps.detail: People Ops finalises the hire (ON-03) with legal entity, work location, scheduled hours and employee class, which fires the eligibility feed to the benefits platform and local brokers. The transaction cannot be approved with work location or hours blank, because those two fields drive most eligibility errors.

steps.label: Determine eligibility and benefit class
steps.detail: Benefits maps the hire to a class (full-time, part-time, intern, variable-hour, expat, fixed-term) under the plan documents and POL-37. US variable-hour and intern populations go into the ACA look-back measurement method rather than being guessed, and anyone expected to work 30+ hours a week is offered coverage within 90 days.
steps.control: Eligibility rules are configured in the platform, not decided case by case.

steps.label: Register statutory schemes from Day 1
steps.detail: TW: Labor, Employment and Occupational Accident Insurance plus NHI effective the first day, and the labor pension report within 7 days. CN: social insurance and housing fund within 30 days on the actual wage base. IN: EPF Form 11/UAN for everyone up to INR 25,000/month and all international workers, ESI up to INR 21,000, plus gratuity and PF nominations. Canada CPP/EI and California SDI start through payroll.
steps.control: Statutory filing receipts saved to the employee record.

steps.label: Open election window and send notices
steps.detail: The benefits platform (US/Canada) or local broker (India/Taiwan/China) opens the new-hire event with a 30-day window and personalised costs. The US packet includes the SBC, COBRA general notice (within 90 days of coverage), HIPAA special enrollment rights, CHIP notice and the 401(k) auto-enrollment/QDIA notice; India shows mediclaim family floater options including optional parents cover.

steps.label: Elect plans and add dependants
steps.detail: Employee elects medical, dental, vision, life/disability, FSA/HSA (US), flex credits (Canada) and 401(k) or group RRSP deferrals, and adds dependants with proof. Dependants' health data is collected with notice and consent (DPDP, PIPL, PDPA), and beneficiaries and nominations are captured in the same session.

steps.label: Elections received by deadline?
steps.detail: Benefits checks incomplete events on day 25 and sends a final reminder; after the window closes the event locks. Late elections wait for open enrollment (BN-02) or a qualifying life event (BN-03).

steps.label: Apply default coverage
steps.detail: Apply plan defaults: employee-only core coverage where the plan document provides it, Canadian mandatory core (basic life, AD&D, LTD), India employee-plus-family floater, and 401(k) auto-enrollment at the default rate for plans subject to IRC 414A. Tell the employee what was defaulted and when they can next change it.

steps.label: Set up deductions and imputed income
steps.detail: Payroll loads pre-tax Section 125 deductions, 401(k) deferrals and imputed income for group-term life over $50,000 and non-tax dependants (US), Canadian taxable benefits for the T4, and India perquisite and NPS treatment. First-payroll deductions are compared with elections before the payroll closes (PY-01).
steps.control: First-payroll deduction-to-election reconciliation.

steps.label: Transmit to carriers and reconcile
steps.detail: The platform sends EDI files to carriers and brokers confirm Canada, India, Taiwan and China supplemental enrollments. Benefits reconciles Darwinbox hires, platform events and carrier acknowledgements weekly and fixes rejects within 5 business days so ID cards arrive before the first claim.

steps.label: Coverage active and confirmed
steps.detail: Employee receives a confirmation statement and ID cards or e-cards, and the record is complete in Darwinbox and the platform. Later issues go to Benefits support, not a new enrollment event.

raci.activity: Statutory registrations (TW, CN, IN, CA SDI, CPP/EI)
Election window, notices and carrier files

controls.control: Weekly three-way reconciliation of Darwinbox hires, benefits platform events and carrier acknowledgements
controls.evidence: Reconciliation report with reject log and resolution dates

controls.control: Statutory enrollment timeliness: TW insurance effective Day 1 and pension report within 7 days; CN social insurance/housing fund within 30 days; IN EPF/ESI in the first contribution cycle
controls.evidence: Filing receipts and monthly exception list reviewed by the Benefits lead

controls.control: Dependant eligibility proof (marriage or birth certificate, partnership affidavit) required before a dependant is covered
controls.evidence: Verification documents in the vendor's restricted repository

controls.control: First-payroll deduction amounts match elections
controls.evidence: Payroll variance report signed off before close

kpis.name: Coverage effective on target date
kpis.why: Gaps create out-of-pocket claims and early-tenure complaints.

kpis.name: Statutory registrations on time
kpis.why: Late TW/CN registration makes the employer liable for lost benefits and back contributions.

kpis.name: Carrier file reject rate
kpis.why: Rejects are the main cause of missing ID cards and denied claims.

considerations: Offer US coverage from date of hire or the first of the following month; anything near the ACA 90-day waiting-period cap looks uncompetitive for engineering hires and adds compliance risk.

Use the ACA look-back measurement method for interns, part-time lab technicians and other variable-hour staff; misclassifying a 30+ hour employee risks 4980H penalties ($3,340 / $5,010 per year in 2026).
401(k) auto-enrollment is mandatory only for plans established after Dec 29, 2022 (IRC 414A); legacy plans can still auto-enroll, which usually lifts participation among early-career engineers.
From 17 Sep 2026 the India EPF mandatory ceiling is INR 25,000/month: update Darwinbox eligibility rules and CTC templates, and remember international workers contribute on full salary from day one.
Collect dependant data once in Darwinbox and push it to vendors; re-keying dependants into broker spreadsheets for India, Taiwan and China is where privacy breaches and coverage errors happen.
In China, commercial supplementary medical cannot replace statutory social insurance and cash in lieu of contributions is void, so never offer an opt-out.

variations.how: Bridge gaps: the BC MSP waiting period (rest of the arrival month plus 2 months) needs interim private cover; Taiwan NHI covers foreign employees with an ARC from the start date; China enrolls foreigners (there is no US-China totalization agreement).

US: an employee returning after a break of less than 13 weeks is treated as continuing for ACA purposes and resumes coverage without a new waiting period; elsewhere restart statutory registration and restore nominations.
Map seller plans to ours, waive waiting periods in supplemental plans and credit deductibles already met where carriers allow.
US: measure hours under the look-back method; Canada, India, Taiwan and China statutory schemes apply regardless of term, and India requires fixed-term parity with permanent staff.

countries.us: Offer affordable minimum-value coverage to at least 95% of full-time (30+ hours) employees with a waiting period of no more than 90 days (2026 affordability 9.96%), and give the SBC, COBRA general notice within 90 days of coverage and HIPAA special enrollment rights (30 days). New 401(k) plans must auto-enroll under IRC 414A.
countries.us-ca: Withhold SDI at 1.3% of all wages (no wage ceiling since 2024), give the DE 2515 and DE 2511 brochures at hire, and file the CalSavers exemption because a 401(k) is offered. SF-based staff trigger HCSO health expenditures, and Bay Area Air District employers with 50+ full-time employees must offer a commuter benefit.
countries.ca: Enrol hires in group benefits on day one (market practice) with extended health, dental, vision, life, AD&D, STD/LTD and EAP; LTD is often employee-paid so benefits are received tax-free. Relocating BC hires face the MSP waiting period (rest of the arrival month plus 2 months), so provide interim private coverage.
countries.in: Enrol EPF (Form 11, UAN, Aadhaar/KYC) for everyone up to INR 25,000/month from 17 Sep 2026 and all international workers, and ESI for employees up to INR 21,000; collect gratuity and PF nominations at joining. Group mediclaim (family floater of INR 5-10 lakh, parents optional) is universal GCC practice and needs consent for dependants' health data.
countries.tw: Enroll Labor Insurance, Employment Insurance, Occupational Accident Insurance and NHI effective the first day of work at the correct insured-salary grade (late enrollment makes the employer liable for lost benefits) and report the labor pension contribution (at least 6%) within 7 days. Supplemental group life, accident and medical cover is expected by candidates comparing TSMC and MediaTek packages.
countries.cn: Register social insurance and housing fund within 30 days in the city of employment on the actual prior-year wage base (Shanghai 2026-27: RMB 7,546-37,731), including foreign employees. Supplementary commercial medical and enterprise annuity are optional add-ons, and any waiver of statutory coverage is void.

processes.name: Annual open enrollment
processes.summary: Runs the annual US open enrollment for the next plan year (November for a January 1 start) and the matching annual re-elections and renewals in Canada, India, Taiwan and China. Covers contribution setting against ACA affordability, loading new IRS limits, required ERISA/ACA notices (SBC, Medicare Part D by Oct 15), decision support, dependant verification and payroll cut-over. Good looks like: notices on time, no deduction errors on the first January payroll, and employees who understand what they chose.
processes.owner: Benefits (process), Total Rewards (plan design and contributions), Payroll (deduction cut-over)
processes.trigger: Renewal decisions approved in BN-05, normally by end of August for a January 1 plan year
outputs: Approved plan-year design and contribution rates with ACA affordability test
Annual notice package with distribution proof (SBC, Part D, CHIP, WHCRA, HIPAA privacy)
Tested platform configuration and new limit tables
Employee elections and dependant verification results
Deduction file for the first payroll of the plan year
processes.sla: Contributions approved by Aug 31; Part D notice by Oct 15; 2-3 week window in November; deductions live on the first January payroll

steps.label: Approve plan design and contributions
steps.detail: Total Rewards takes renewal results from BN-05 and sets employee contributions by tier; the lowest-cost self-only option is tested against next year's ACA affordability percentage (2026: 9.96%; confirm the 2027 figure). CHRO and Finance approve, and any benefit reduction is flagged for early communication.
steps.control: Documented affordability test before rates are approved.

steps.label: Load new plan-year limits
steps.detail: Load the 2027 IRS limits when published (verify each figure; 2026 reference: 401(k) $24,500, catch-up $8,000, ages 60-63 $11,250, HSA $4,400/$8,750, health FSA $3,400 with $680 carryover, dependent care FSA $7,500 and not indexed). Confirm the Roth catch-up flag for employees whose prior-year FICA wages exceed the threshold ($150,000 for 2025 wages, indexed).

steps.label: Configure and test OE platform
steps.detail: Vendor configures plans, rates, eligibility and EDI changes; Benefits runs test cases (new hire, part-timer, employee on leave, HSA with general FSA conflict, domestic partner imputed income) and signs off UAT before the window opens.
steps.control: UAT sign-off before go-live.

steps.label: Distribute notices and decision support
steps.detail: Send the Medicare Part D creditable coverage notice by Oct 15, plus SBCs, CHIP, WHCRA and wellness notices and the HIPAA privacy notice when due (every 3 years). Run webinars, an HSA/HDHP cost modeller and FAQs, and mail packets to employees on leave.

steps.label: Make elections in window
steps.detail: Employees review and elect during a 2-3 week window; FSA and HSA contributions need active re-election, while other plans roll over in a passive year. Changes after close need a qualifying life event (BN-03).

steps.label: New dependants added?
steps.detail: The platform flags every newly added spouse, partner or child for verification before the plan year starts.

steps.label: Verify dependant eligibility
steps.detail: Vendor requests proof (marriage certificate, birth certificate, tax return) with a 30-45 day deadline and drops unverified dependants prospectively with notice. Run a full-population audit every 3 years rather than every year.

steps.label: Audit elections and carrier files
steps.detail: Benefits reviews exception reports (HSA with a general-purpose FSA, tiers inconsistent with dependants, missing Roth catch-up coding, carrier rejects) and has the vendor correct them before confirmation statements go out.

steps.label: Load plan-year deductions
steps.detail: Payroll loads the new deduction file for the first payroll of the plan year and compares totals with the prior year by plan and tier; variances above tolerance are investigated before close (PY-01).
steps.control: First-payroll deduction reconciliation.

steps.label: New plan-year coverage live
steps.detail: Confirmation statements issue and ID cards are reissued where carriers changed. A short pulse on clarity feeds next year's communication plan.

controls.control: ACA affordability test of the lowest-cost self-only premium before contributions are approved
Annual notice calendar with proof of distribution (Part D by Oct 15; CMS creditable coverage disclosure within 60 days of plan year start)
UAT sign-off of platform configuration and limits before the window opens
Reconciliation of elections to first-payroll deductions

kpis.name: Election/deduction error rate
kpis.why: January errors create retro deductions and erode trust.

kpis.name: Notices distributed on time
kpis.why: Late Part D or SBC notices carry penalties and audit findings.

kpis.name: New dependants verified or removed
kpis.why: Ineligible dependants are a direct cost leak.

kpis.name: Employee understanding of benefits (pulse)
kpis.why: Use of HSA and wellbeing offerings depends on comprehension.

considerations: As of Sept 2026 some 2027 limits may not be published; build the platform with placeholders and reload within 5 business days of IRS release rather than delaying the window.

2027 is the first plan year under the final Roth catch-up regulations (good-faith compliance covered 2026): use deemed Roth elections for catch-ups above the FICA wage threshold, and make payroll pass prior-year W-2 Box 3 wages to the recordkeeper.
Passive enrollment is fine in a stable year, but force active enrollment when changing carriers or plan designs; it also cleans stale dependant data.
Engineer-heavy populations pick HDHP/HSA plans when modellers show tax savings; pair the modeller with out-of-pocket examples to avoid surprise complaints later.
Put non-US re-elections (Canada flex credits, India parental top-ups) in the same calendar so data freezes and communications are coordinated.

variations.how: Run active enrollment, reissue ID cards and give new SBCs; material mid-year SBC changes need 60 days' advance notice, and an SMM is due within 210 days after the plan year ends.
Annual flex-credit re-election, with taxable-benefit coding checked for the T4 (employer-paid life and lifestyle spending accounts).
Re-elect parental cover and top-ups at the policy renewal date, update dependants and collect consent for dependants' health data.
Send the packet to personal contact details; elections take effect normally and premiums follow the LV-01 arrangement.

countries.us: Send the Medicare Part D creditable coverage notice by Oct 15 plus SBC, CHIP, WHCRA and (every 3 years) HIPAA privacy notices, and recheck ACA affordability against next year's percentage. Load new HSA, FSA, dependent care FSA ($7,500 from 2026, not indexed) and 401(k) limits and confirm Roth catch-up coding.
countries.us-ca: California open enrollment runs October-November; check the CalSavers exemption and SF HCSO expenditure rates at each renewal. Self-insured plans file Forms 1094/1095 with the Franchise Tax Board by 31 March for the state individual mandate.
countries.ca: There is no statutory open enrollment; flex or credit-based plans re-elect annually, and employer-paid group term life and lifestyle spending accounts are taxable benefits on the T4 (private health and dental premiums are taxable only in Quebec).
countries.in: Group mediclaim re-election (parents, top-ups) follows the policy renewal date, and the April tax-regime choice decides whether employer NPS contributions (up to 14%) and old-regime allowances are worth electing.
countries.tw: Statutory schemes have no open enrollment; supplemental group insurance renews annually, and MOL/NHIA publish next year's insured-salary grade tables in November for loading on January 1.
countries.cn: There is no open enrollment; social insurance and housing fund bases reset each July (Shanghai 2026-27 base RMB 7,546-37,731, retroactive top-ups due by 30 Sept 2026), and supplementary medical and enterprise annuity renew annually.

processes.name: Qualifying life events
processes.summary: Processes mid-year benefit changes after a qualifying life event (marriage, birth or adoption, divorce, death of a dependant, loss or gain of other coverage, relocation). Applies the Section 125 consistency rule and HIPAA special enrollment windows in the US and the equivalent carrier and statutory updates elsewhere. Good looks like: newborns covered from birth, changes processed within 5 business days of complete proof, and linked leave or COBRA steps triggered automatically.
processes.owner: Benefits (process), benefits administration vendor (US processing), People Ops (non-US dependant and nomination records)
processes.trigger: Employee reports an event in the benefits platform or Darwinbox, or a Darwinbox change (marital status, address) flags a possible event
outputs: Approved or denied life-event record with supporting documents
Updated elections and dependants with effective dates
Retro deduction or refund in payroll
Updated beneficiaries and statutory nominations (PF, gratuity)
Linked triggers: leave case (LV-01), COBRA notice (BN-06), death process (OF-09)
processes.sla: Employee reports within 30 days (60 days for Medicaid/CHIP events); processed within 5 business days of complete documentation

steps.label: Report life event within window
steps.detail: Employee reports the event and its date in the benefits platform (US) or Darwinbox (other countries), normally within 30 days (60 days for Medicaid/CHIP events). Darwinbox changes to marital status or address prompt the employee to check whether a benefits event applies.

steps.label: Validate event and requested change
steps.detail: Vendor checks that the event is a permitted change under the cafeteria plan (Treas. Reg. 1.125-4) and that the requested change is consistent with it, for example adding a spouse after marriage but not dropping an unrelated plan. HSA contribution changes are allowed at any time prospectively.

steps.label: Documentation valid and timely?
steps.detail: Vendor reviews proof and dates; pending events stay open for up to 30 days for missing documents.

steps.label: Submit missing documents
steps.detail: Employee uploads the certificate, court order or loss-of-coverage letter. If nothing arrives within 30 days the event is denied and the next opportunity is open enrollment.

steps.label: Process elections and effective dates
steps.detail: Birth, adoption or placement coverage is retroactive to the event date when elected within 30 days; other changes are usually effective the first of the month after the request. Vendor updates carriers by EDI and issues a confirmation statement.

steps.label: Update non-US dependants and nominations
steps.detail: Canada: add or remove dependants and beneficiaries with the carrier within the contract window. India: add spouse or newborn to the mediclaim floater and update PF e-nomination and gratuity nomination on marriage. Taiwan: add or remove NHI dependants. China: update supplementary commercial cover, since statutory employee medical insurance generally covers only the employee (verify local children's schemes).

steps.label: Adjust deductions and retro amounts
steps.detail: Payroll applies new deduction amounts and any retro catch-up or refund, spread per policy, and updates imputed income for non-tax dependants such as domestic partners (US).
steps.control: Retro adjustments covering more than 2 pay periods reviewed by Benefits.

steps.label: Trigger linked processes
steps.detail: Birth or adoption opens a leave case (LV-01: FMLA/CFRA bonding, PFL, EI, Taiwan parental leave, China maternity insurance). Divorce or a child aging out starts the COBRA path (BN-06), and the death of an employee or dependant routes to OF-09 and life insurance claims.

steps.label: Coverage updated and confirmed
steps.detail: Employee receives the confirmation statement and new ID cards where needed; the dependant record in Darwinbox matches the carrier.

steps.label: Change denied with next opportunity
steps.detail: Employee receives a written denial with the reason (late, inconsistent or unsupported) and the next chance to change (open enrollment or a future event); appeals go to the Benefits lead.

raci.activity: Non-US dependant, beneficiary and nomination updates
Linked leave, COBRA and death triggers

controls.control: Consistency-rule and deadline check before any mid-year change is approved
controls.evidence: Event record with documents and approver

controls.control: Monthly review of retro deductions or refunds spanning more than 2 pay periods
controls.evidence: Payroll retro report with Benefits sign-off

controls.control: Divorce and age-out events passed to the COBRA administrator promptly after the employee's notice

kpis.name: Processing time from complete proof
kpis.why: Delays leave families uninsured when they need care.

kpis.name: Newborns covered from date of birth
kpis.why: Retroactive birth coverage is a legal right and a trust moment.

kpis.name: Denials overturned on appeal
kpis.why: A high overturn rate means rules or communications are unclear.

considerations: Communicate the 30-day clock when the event happens, not only in the SPD: tie reminders to Darwinbox marital-status and address changes and to leave requests for birth or adoption.
Apply the consistency rule strictly but explain it; a one-line reason plus the next opportunity cuts escalations from engineers who challenge denials.
A move between countries is a transfer (MV-03), not a US life event: end home-country coverage and enroll in host-country plans without a gap.
Keep dependant documents in the vendor's restricted repository, not in email or Darwinbox attachments visible to HRBPs.

variations.how: Coverage is retroactive to the event date if elected within 30 days; the event also opens LV-01 bonding or parental leave and, in Taiwan and China, statutory leave and insurance claims.
Remove the spouse from the end of the month of the decree; the employee must notify within 60 days to preserve the former spouse's 36-month COBRA right.
Special enrollment within 30 days of the loss with proof of the loss date; coverage starts the first of the following month.
Route to OF-09; dependants get a 36-month COBRA offer in the US and life insurance claims start on carrier forms.

countries.us: Section 125 allows mid-year changes only for permitted events consistent with the change, and HIPAA special enrollment gives 30 days (60 days for Medicaid/CHIP) with birth or adoption coverage retroactive to the event. Divorce or a child aging out needs employee notice within 60 days to preserve COBRA.
countries.us-ca: Birth or adoption usually also triggers PDL/CFRA and an EDD PFL claim (route to LV-01), and California insured plans must cover registered domestic partners on the same terms as spouses (verify with the carrier).
countries.ca: Carriers typically require dependant additions within 31 days or treat them as late applicants needing medical evidence (verify the contract); update life insurance beneficiaries at the same time.
countries.in: Update PF e-nomination and gratuity nomination on marriage and add a spouse or newborn to the mediclaim family floater within the insurer's window, with consent for dependants' health details.
countries.tw: Add or remove NHI dependants through the employer's insurance unit; childbirth also triggers maternity, paternity and parental leave and a Labor Insurance childbirth benefit claim (verify amount).
countries.cn: Statutory employee medical insurance generally does not cover dependants (verify local children's schemes), so update supplementary commercial cover; marriage and childbirth trigger marriage leave (Shanghai 10 days) and maternity insurance claims.

processes.name: Retirement plan governance
processes.summary: Governs the company's retirement plans as a fiduciary: the US 401(k) committee, investment and fee oversight, plan operation (deferrals, limits, testing), filings and disclosures, and oversight of non-US retirement and gratuity arrangements. Covers SECURE 2.0 changes including mandatory Roth catch-up from 2026 and auto-enrollment for new plans, Canada group RRSP/DPSP, India PF and gratuity funding, Taiwan labor pension and China enterprise annuity. Good looks like: a documented prudent process, zero late deposits and clean testing and filings.
processes.owner: Retirement plan committee (fiduciary, chaired by the CFO), Total Rewards (plan sponsor administration), Benefits (non-US plans)
processes.trigger: Quarterly committee cycle and the annual compliance calendar (plan year end, testing, Form 5500), plus any law change or plan event
outputs: Committee charter, quarterly minutes and investment policy statement reviews
Fee benchmarking and 404a-5 participant disclosures
Nondiscrimination and limit testing results with corrections
Form 5500 with audit report and Summary Annual Report
Plan amendments and participant notices
Annual non-US plan review (RRSP/DPSP, PF and gratuity valuation, TW pension, CN annuity)
processes.sla: Committee meets quarterly; deferrals remitted within 3 business days of payday (target); Form 5500 by Jul 31 (Oct 15 with Form 5558)

steps.label: Convene quarterly plan committee
steps.detail: Total Rewards schedules the committee (CFO chair, Controller, CHRO delegate, Legal) under its charter with a standing agenda: investments, fees, operations, compliance and legal updates. Members complete fiduciary training on appointment and every 2 years.

steps.label: Deliver investment and fee reports
steps.detail: The 3(21) or 3(38) adviser and the recordkeeper report fund performance against the IPS, watch-list status, fee benchmarks, participation and deferral statistics. A recordkeeping RFP or formal benchmark runs at least every 3 years.

steps.label: Review funds, fees and operations
steps.detail: The committee reviews reports, operational exceptions (late deposits, loan defaults, missed deferrals) and legal changes, and records its reasoning in the minutes; a documented process is the fiduciary defense.
steps.control: Minutes record each decision and its rationale.

steps.label: Changes to plan or lineup needed?
steps.detail: Decision covers fund changes, fee renegotiation, plan design (match, safe harbor, Roth, auto-escalation) and required legal amendments.

steps.label: Amend plan and notify participants
steps.detail: Legal drafts amendments (including SECURE 2.0 conforming amendments by the applicable deadline; verify) for Board or delegate approval. Participants receive an SMM, fund-change or QDIA notice (30 days) and a blackout notice at least 30 days before any recordkeeper conversion.

steps.label: Remit deferrals and code catch-ups
steps.detail: Payroll remits deferrals and loan repayments as soon as they can be segregated (target within 3 business days of payday), applies the 2026 limits ($24,500 deferral, $8,000 catch-up, $11,250 at ages 60-63) and routes catch-ups as Roth for employees whose prior-year FICA wages exceeded $150,000.
steps.control: Deposit timeliness checked every payroll.

steps.label: Run nondiscrimination and limit tests
steps.detail: The recordkeeper runs ADP/ACP, top-heavy, 402(g) and 415(c) tests using the $160,000 HCE threshold and the plan's compensation definition. Failed tests are corrected within 2.5 months after plan year end to avoid excise tax, unless the plan uses a safe harbor design.

steps.label: Complete plan audit and Form 5500
steps.detail: Finance engages the plan auditor (required for large plans with 100+ participants) and files Form 5500 by July 31, or October 15 with Form 5558; the Summary Annual Report follows, and the recordkeeper's SOC 1 Type II report is reviewed.

steps.label: Oversee non-US retirement plans
steps.detail: Annual review of Canada group RRSP/DPSP (match, DPSP vesting of no more than 2 years, 60-day contribution deadline), India PF remittance by the 15th and gratuity trust or insurer funding with actuarial valuation, Taiwan 6% labor pension and old-system reserve top-up by 31 March, and any China enterprise annuity. Results go to the committee once a year.

steps.label: Minutes and filings archived
steps.detail: Minutes, reports, amendments, test results and filings are kept in document management for at least 6 years (ERISA), and open actions roll into the next agenda.

raci.activity: Fiduciary oversight of investments and fees

controls.control: Deferral and loan remittance date compared with payday every payroll; late deposits escalated for correction
Committee meets at least quarterly with minutes, IPS review and annual fee benchmarking
Annual mapping of the plan's compensation definition to payroll earnings codes (RSU/ESPP income, bonuses, sign-on)
controls.evidence: Earnings-code map signed by Payroll and Total Rewards

controls.control: Review of the recordkeeper's SOC 1 Type II report and complementary user-entity controls

kpis.name: Late deposits
kpis.why: Late deferrals are prohibited transactions that need correction and Form 5500 disclosure.

kpis.name: Participation rate
kpis.why: Shows plan effectiveness and helps pass ADP/ACP testing.

kpis.name: All-in plan cost
kpis.target: At or below peer median in benchmark
kpis.why: Excessive fees are the most common fiduciary litigation theory.

kpis.name: Corrective refunds from testing
kpis.why: Refunds to HCE engineers are a visible dissatisfier.

considerations: Equity-heavy pay is the main operational trap: decide explicitly whether RSU and ESPP income is plan compensation and make payroll earnings codes match the plan document, or every vest becomes an operational failure.
An HCE-heavy engineering workforce often fails ADP/ACP; a safe harbor match is usually cheaper than annual refunds and lets HCEs defer the maximum.

Mandatory Roth catch-up (IRC 414(v)(7)) needs payroll to pass prior-year FICA wages (W-2 Box 3) to the recordkeeper, and a plan without a Roth feature cannot offer catch-ups to those employees at all.
Auto-enrollment is mandatory only for 401(k) plans established after Dec 29, 2022 (IRC 414A); check any plan acquired or created in a transaction.

Non-US plans are not ERISA plans but still need governance: India gratuity liabilities must be revalued on the Code 'wages' base, and a China enterprise annuity needs collective consultation before adoption.

variations.how: Blackout notice at least 30 days ahead, fund-mapping or QDIA notice, and a balance reconciliation after conversion.
Decide merge versus terminate before closing, since terminating afterwards triggers successor-plan limits, and plan the testing transition.
Correct under EPCRS (self-correction where eligible) and record the correction in the minutes.
Review treaty treatment of 401(k) and RRSP contributions and any certificate of coverage before continuing home-plan participation.

countries.us: Maintain the ERISA plan document and SPD (SMM within 210 days after plan year end), fiduciary charter, minutes, fee benchmarking and 404a-5 disclosures, and file Form 5500 by July 31. 2026 limits are $24,500 deferral, $8,000 catch-up ($11,250 at 60-63), 415(c) $72,000, 401(a)(17) $360,000 and HCE $160,000, with Roth catch-up required above $150,000 of prior-year FICA wages (final regulations generally from 2027).
countries.us-ca: Because a qualified 401(k) is offered, file the CalSavers exemption to stop penalty notices; plan governance otherwise follows federal ERISA.
countries.ca: Group RRSP with a DPSP match (commonly 50-100% of contributions up to 3-6% of salary) and DPSP vesting of no more than 2 years; RRSP room is 18% of prior-year earnings up to the annual limit (verify 2026), and prior-year contributions must be remitted by the 60-day deadline (about Mar 1-2).
countries.in: EPF is 12% + 12% of 'wages' with EPS capped at INR 2,083/month on INR 25,000 from 17 Sep 2026, deposited by the 15th; gratuity (15 days' wages per completed year after 5 years, 1 year for fixed-term, ceiling INR 20 lakh) should be funded through a trust or insurer and valued annually on the Code wages base.
countries.tw: Contribute at least 6% of monthly wage (wage cap NT$150,000) to each eligible employee's Labor Pension individual account and report within 7 days of hire or separation; top up any old-system reserve shortfall by 31 March and confirm coverage for foreign professionals under the 2025 amendments.
countries.cn: Basic pension runs through social insurance (Shanghai employer share about 16%); an enterprise annuity is optional, must pass collective consultation, and is capped at 8% of payroll for the employer and 12% combined (verify the 2018 Measures).

processes.name: Global benefits renewal & vendor management
processes.summary: Manages the annual renewal of all group benefit contracts and the lifecycle of benefits vendors (brokers, carriers, TPAs, benefits platform, EAP, retirement providers) across the six jurisdictions. Covers experience review, benchmarking, renew-or-market decisions, contract and data-protection terms, budget approval and ongoing service oversight. Good looks like: renewals decided 60+ days before the effective date, cost trend at or below market, and every vendor under a signed DPA with measured service levels.
processes.owner: Benefits (process), Total Rewards (strategy and decision), Legal and Security (contract and data terms), Finance (budget)
processes.trigger: Renewal calendar: 150 days before each contract's effective date, or a vendor performance or pricing issue
outputs: Renewal analysis with claims experience and market benchmark per country
Renew/market decision memo and approved budget
Executed contracts, DPAs/BAAs and broker compensation disclosures
Implementation plan feeding open enrollment (BN-02)
Quarterly vendor scorecards and vendor register
processes.sla: Decision 90 days before effective date; contracts signed 60 days before; quarterly scorecards

steps.label: Launch renewal by country
steps.detail: Benefits opens each renewal 150 days before the effective date from a global calendar (US January 1; Canada, India, Taiwan and China by policy year), confirms census data from Darwinbox and briefs brokers on objectives.

steps.label: Deliver experience and renewal quotes
steps.detail: Brokers deliver claims experience, large claims, trend, carrier renewal offers and peer benchmarks for the markets we actually hire in: Bay Area chip and big tech, Canadian tech, Bengaluru GCCs, TSMC and MediaTek in Taiwan, and MNC tech in Shanghai and Shenzhen.

steps.label: Model options and competitiveness
steps.detail: Benefits models plan design, contribution and funding options (fully insured versus self-funded with stop-loss in the US) and competitive position, and flags any change that reduces benefits for early communication.

steps.label: Renew or go to market?
steps.detail: Total Rewards decides using price, service history, competitiveness and time since the last market test.

steps.label: Run RFP and select carrier
steps.detail: The broker runs the RFP with standard questions on price, network, service, data security and implementation; finalists present and Benefits scores them with Security and Legal input. Test the market every 3-5 years even when renewals look fine.

steps.label: Negotiate contract, DPA and security terms
steps.detail: Legal and Security require a DPA (a HIPAA BAA for US health vendors), SOC 1 or SOC 2 reports, breach-notice terms, PIPL entrusted-processing terms and a cross-border mechanism for China, DPDP-ready terms for India, CAA broker compensation disclosure, and screening against DOJ Data Security Program covered-person rules.
steps.control: No employee data leaves our systems before the DPA and security review are complete.

steps.label: Approve budget and accruals
steps.detail: FP&A and Finance approve the per-country cost and accruals; increases above budget tolerance go to the CHRO and CFO.

steps.label: Implement and communicate changes
steps.detail: Benefits signs contracts by e-signature, updates plan setup in Darwinbox and the platform, EDI feeds and local enrollment files, and hands employee communications to BN-02 (US) or local HR teams.

steps.label: Monitor vendor SLAs quarterly
steps.detail: Quarterly scorecards cover claim turnaround, service-center performance, accuracy, escalations and data incidents; repeated misses trigger remediation plans and fee holdbacks where the contract allows.

steps.label: Renewal documented and filed
steps.detail: Decision memo, contracts, disclosures and scorecards are filed in document management and summarized in Total Rewards' annual benefits review.

controls.control: Broker and consultant compensation disclosed in writing before contracting (CAA 2021 for US group health plans)
DPA/BAA executed and security review passed before any employee data is sent to a vendor
controls.evidence: Security review ticket and signed DPA

controls.control: Each country's main contracts competitively tested at least every 5 years, or a waiver documented
controls.evidence: Vendor register with last market-test date

controls.control: Gifts and hospitality from brokers and carriers logged and pre-approved above threshold

kpis.name: Renewal cost trend vs market trend
kpis.target: At or below broker-reported market trend
kpis.why: Shows negotiation and plan management value.

kpis.name: Renewals decided on time
kpis.target: 100% at least 60 days before effective date
kpis.why: Late decisions compress communication and enrollment.

kpis.name: Vendor SLA attainment
kpis.why: Service failures land on employees and HR.

considerations: Benchmark against the market each site actually competes in, not a global average: TSMC and MediaTek in Hsinchu, other GCCs in Bengaluru, Bay Area chip and big tech in California.

Data flows are the hidden risk: China employee data leaving the country needs PIPL notice, separate consent, a PIPIA and a transfer mechanism, and US bulk personal data must not reach vendors that are covered persons under the DOJ Data Security Program.
For a self-funded US plan, write RxDC (Jun 1), PCORI (Jul 31) and MHPAEA NQTL analyses into the TPA's contract deliverables rather than assuming the TPA handles them.
Once premiums are large enough, consider multinational pooling for group life, disability and medical across Canada, India, Taiwan and China; pool dividends offset renewal increases.
Keep one vendor register with contract dates, DPA status, SOC report dates and owners; it doubles as SOX evidence for payroll-adjacent vendors.

variations.how: Set up statutory schemes first, then supplemental cover through the pooling network or a local broker, with DPA and data residency confirmed.
Emergency marketing through the broker, continuity-of-care letters and a special enrollment if plan options change.
Inventory acquired plans and contracts, keep them through the current plan year, then harmonize at the next renewal.
Renew stop-loss and TPA together, review large-claim lasers, and update the plan document and SBC.

countries.us: Obtain CAA broker compensation disclosures and SOC reports; self-funded plans file RxDC by June 1, pay PCORI by July 31 and keep MHPAEA NQTL comparative analyses, and Forms 1094-C/1095-C are e-filed by March 31.
countries.us-ca: Insured plans follow California mandates and Cal-COBRA rules for small groups, and the renewal checklist should include SF HCSO expenditure rates and the Bay Area commuter benefit.
countries.ca: Benchmark extended health, dental, paramedical and mental health (often C$1,000-2,500+), life, STD/LTD, EAP and HSA/LSA, and confirm carrier contracts allow continuation through ESA and common-law notice periods; a qualifying STD plan may earn an EI premium reduction (verify).
countries.in: Renew group mediclaim (family floater INR 5-10 lakh, parents optional), term life and accident or employee compensation cover against GCC norms, and update vendor contracts for DPDP duties that start on 13 May 2027.
countries.tw: Supplemental group life, accident and medical insurance and enhanced health checks are expected; festival gifts and bonuses run through the Employee Welfare Committee, not the insurance budget.
countries.cn: Supplementary medical and enterprise annuity vendors process sensitive PI, so contracts need PIPL entrusted-processing terms, a PIPIA and a cross-border mechanism (standard contract or certification) for data sent to the US.

processes.name: Benefits continuation (COBRA)
processes.summary: Continues health coverage for employees and dependants who lose eligibility (termination, reduced hours, divorce, age-out, death) through COBRA, Cal-COBRA and non-US equivalents, including severance-funded premium subsidies. Covers timely notices, election and premium administration, and conversion or portability outside the US. Good looks like: every qualifying event noticed within the statutory window, subsidies matching the separation agreement, and no surprise coverage gaps.
processes.owner: Benefits (process), COBRA administrator (notices and administration), Payroll (subsidy funding), People Ops (event data)
processes.trigger: Qualifying event: termination other than for gross misconduct, reduction in hours, death, divorce or legal separation, dependant aging out, Medicare entitlement
outputs: Qualifying event notice to the administrator
COBRA/Cal-COBRA election notice plus HIPP and LC 2800.2 notices (California)
Election and premium payment records
Severance subsidy setup matching the separation agreement
Non-US continuation, conversion and statutory withdrawal records
processes.sla: Employer to administrator within 30 days; election notice within 14 days (44 days if employer-administered); 60-day election window

steps.label: Record qualifying event in Darwinbox
steps.detail: People Ops records the termination, hours change or death with the correct reason and coverage end date (normally the end of the month), which feeds the benefits platform nightly. Divorce and age-out events come from the employee or the platform (BN-03).

steps.label: Notify COBRA administrator
steps.detail: Benefits confirms the event reached the administrator and submits manual events within 30 days of the qualifying event. The gross-misconduct exclusion is rarely used and needs Legal sign-off.
steps.control: Weekly reconciliation of terminations to COBRA events.

steps.label: Send election notice
steps.detail: The administrator sends the COBRA election notice within 14 days (44 days in total when the employer administers) with premiums (up to 102%) and deadlines. In California add Cal-COBRA terms for small insured plans, the HIPP notice and the LC 2800.2 continuation and conversion notice.

steps.label: Severance includes premium subsidy?
steps.detail: Benefits checks the signed separation agreement or severance plan (OF-04) for subsidy months, tiers and early-end terms.

steps.label: Set up severance subsidy
steps.detail: Payroll and Benefits set up the subsidy exactly as the agreement states (months, tiers, early end on new coverage), paid either as employer premiums to the administrator or as a taxable cash equivalent, and diarize the end date.
steps.control: Subsidy terms checked line by line against the signed agreement.

steps.label: Elect coverage and pay premiums
steps.detail: Qualified beneficiaries have 60 days from the later of loss of coverage or the notice to elect, 45 days after election for the first premium and a 30-day grace period for later premiums; coverage is retroactive once paid.

steps.label: Administer coverage and end dates
steps.detail: The administrator tracks the 18, 29 (disability) or 36-month maximum, collects premiums and sends early-termination notices when coverage ends for non-payment, new group coverage or the maximum period.

steps.label: Run non-US continuation and conversion
steps.detail: Canada: continue benefits through the Ontario ESA notice period, then communicate life and health conversion deadlines. India: mediclaim ends at exit, so share insurer portability options. Taiwan: withdraw insurances on the last day. China: transfer or suspend social insurance and housing fund within 15 days.

steps.label: Continuation elected or expired
steps.detail: The record closes when the beneficiary waives, the election period lapses or maximum coverage ends; documents are kept under POL-49.

raci.activity: Qualifying event capture and administrator notice
Non-US continuation, conversion and statutory withdrawal

controls.control: Weekly reconciliation of Darwinbox terminations and hours changes to COBRA events
Election notice timeliness tracked against the 44-day limit with proof of mailing
Severance subsidy setup matched to the signed separation agreement before the first payment

kpis.name: Election notices within statutory window
kpis.why: Late notices carry per-day penalties and extend claim exposure.

kpis.name: Subsidy setup accuracy
kpis.why: Errors breach separation agreements and start disputes.

kpis.name: Substantiated coverage gaps reported by former employees
kpis.why: Gaps at exit damage the employer brand and create claims.

considerations: Paying the subsidy as a taxable cash equivalent is simpler and avoids nondiscrimination questions for self-insured plans under IRC 105(h) (verify with benefits counsel); always stop the subsidy when new group coverage starts.
Align end dates across medical, dental, vision and FSA; end of month is kinder and easier to administer than the termination date.
In a RIF, bulk-load events and check that WARN pay-in-lieu periods, subsidy periods and coverage end dates line up.
In Canada the real risk is LTD during the common-law notice period; confirm the carrier allows continuation or price the uninsured risk into the settlement.
Managers should never promise coverage terms in exit conversations; point to the notice and the Benefits contact.

variations.how: Bulk event file, uniform subsidy terms in the RIF package, and Cal-WARN benefits exposure checked if notice is short.
Dependants receive a 36-month COBRA offer; many employers subsidize 3-6 months as bereavement support.
A beneficiary determined disabled by SSA within the first 60 days of COBRA gets 29 months, at up to 150% of cost for months 19-29.
Continue benefits through statutory notice (Ontario), negotiate longer continuation in settlements, then issue conversion notices.

countries.us: COBRA applies at 20+ employees: the employer notifies the administrator within 30 days, the election notice goes out within 14 days (44 if employer-administered), the election window is 60 days and coverage lasts 18/29/36 months. Add the 402(f) rollover notice, FSA run-out, HSA portability and life and disability conversion information.
countries.us-ca: Cal-COBRA covers insured plans with 2-19 employees, and at termination the HIPP notice and LC 2800.2 continuation/conversion notice go out with the UI Code 1089 notice of change in employment status.
countries.ca: The Ontario ESA requires benefit plan contributions to continue through the statutory notice period and common-law damages include benefits for reasonable notice; communicate life and health conversion deadlines from the carrier contract.
countries.in: There is no statutory health continuation, so mediclaim ends at exit; pay full and final settlement within 2 working days and gratuity within 30 days, and support PF transfer or withdrawal.
countries.tw: Withdraw Labor Insurance, Employment Insurance, occupational accident insurance and NHI on the last day and report the pension stop within 7 days; issue the involuntary separation certificate for Employment Insurance benefits on Art. 11 or 13 exits.
countries.cn: Transfer or suspend social insurance and housing fund within 15 days of termination (LCL Art. 50) alongside the termination certificate; supplementary commercial medical ends under the policy terms.

processes.name: Leave of absence
processes.summary: One front door for every leave of absence: employees ask once (US through the leave vendor, other countries through Darwinbox), and the leave team determines eligibility across all overlapping regimes, certifies and designates the leave, coordinates pay with statutory benefits, continues benefits and equity, protects the job and plans the return. Covers US federal and state leaves (FMLA, CFRA, PDL, PFL/SDI, bereavement, reproductive loss, USERRA), Canadian ESA leaves with EI, India maternity, Taiwan's day- and hour-based leaves and China's maternity and medical treatment periods. Good looks like: notices on time, no pay or benefit errors, zero leave-related retaliation findings and a planned return.
processes.owner: Benefits - Leave & Accommodation team (process), leave vendor (US administration), Payroll (pay), HRBP (job protection and reinstatement)
processes.trigger: Employee request (30 days' notice where foreseeable), manager or HR awareness of a possible qualifying reason, or a work injury that also qualifies
outputs: Eligibility and rights notice for each applicable regime
Certification on file in a restricted medical record
Designation notice with concurrent-leave mapping and dates
Darwinbox leave status and payroll instructions (paid/unpaid, top-up, statutory offsets)
Benefits continuation and premium arrangement
Return-to-work plan and reinstatement confirmation
processes.sla: Eligibility/rights notice within 5 business days of the request; designation within 5 business days of complete certification; pay set up before the first affected payroll

steps.label: Request leave through single intake
steps.detail: Employee requests leave through the vendor portal or phone line (US) or the Darwinbox leave module (Canada, India, Taiwan, China), with 30 days' notice where foreseeable. Managers who learn of a possible qualifying reason route it to intake within 2 business days; the employee never has to name the law.

steps.label: Screen eligibility across all regimes
steps.detail: US: the vendor tests FMLA (50 employees within 75 miles, 12 months, 1,250 hours), CFRA and PDL (5+ employees), state PFML and sick leave, bereavement, reproductive loss and USERRA against the work location. Elsewhere the leave team applies Ontario/BC ESA, the SS Code, Taiwan LSA and Gender Equality in Employment Act, and PRC national plus Shanghai/Shenzhen rules configured in Darwinbox.

steps.label: Send eligibility and rights notice
steps.detail: Issue the eligibility and rights-and-responsibilities notice within 5 business days, stating the certification required, premium obligations and any fitness-for-duty requirement. Non-US entitlements are confirmed in writing through Darwinbox (for example India's maternity benefit terms or Taiwan leave approval).
steps.control: Notice timeliness tracked in the vendor SLA report.

steps.label: Certification required?
steps.detail: Medical or supporting certification is needed for own or family serious health conditions and long illness leaves, but not for bereavement, bonding with proof of birth, or obvious short needs.

steps.label: Return certification
steps.detail: Employee returns provider certification within 15 calendar days (FMLA/CFRA; CFRA certification cannot demand the diagnosis), a practitioner certificate for Ontario long-term illness leave, or local medical or birth documents. Ontario cannot require a note for the 3 ESA sick days and BC cannot for short absences; certifications go only to the vendor or the restricted Darwinbox folder.

steps.label: Statutory entitlement available?
steps.detail: The leave team confirms remaining entitlement in each regime; exhausted or ineligible cases are never closed without an accommodation review.

steps.label: Designate leave and confirm dates
steps.detail: Issue the designation notice within 5 business days of complete information, mapping concurrent regimes (FMLA with CFRA; PDL not concurrent with CFRA; PFL is wage replacement, not job protection), the amount counted and any intermittent schedule. Managers see dates and status only.

steps.label: Plan coverage without medical detail
steps.detail: Manager plans work coverage, delegations and approvals (including export-controlled project access and on-call rotations) and agrees contact preferences. No work requests during leave and no questions about the condition.

steps.label: Coordinate pay with statutory benefits
steps.detail: Payroll sets paid or unpaid status and company top-ups so nobody is overpaid: integrate with California SDI/PFL (vacation cannot be required first), top up Canadian EI only through the registered SUB plan and file the ROE within 5 calendar days, apply ESI for covered India staff, Taiwan's Employment Insurance parental allowance and China maternity allowance, with employer top-up to salary where required.
steps.control: Leave pay changes reviewed by a second payroll analyst.

steps.label: Continue benefits and collect premiums
steps.detail: Group health continues on the same terms during FMLA, CFRA, PDL and USERRA (up to 24 months), with arrears or direct billing for unpaid periods. Canada continues benefit contributions and seniority unless the employee opts out; Taiwan parental leave lets the employee keep social insurance with premium relief and deferral (verify), and China statutory insurance continues.

steps.label: Apply equity vesting leave rules
steps.detail: Stock Admin records the leave in the equity platform: vesting continues during statutory and company-paid leave, and any tolling for long non-statutory personal leave follows the plan and local counsel (never for Canadian ESA leaves). Check blackout and 10b5-1 timing for insiders going on leave.

steps.label: Extension requested or leave exhausted?
steps.detail: Vendor or leave team monitors usage, recertification dates and extension requests two weeks before the scheduled end.

steps.label: Assess extended leave as accommodation
steps.detail: Before any action at exhaustion, HRBP and the leave team run the accommodation process (LV-02): the ADA and FEHA treat finite extra leave as a possible accommodation, and Canadian human rights law requires accommodation to undue hardship. Approved extensions go back to designation; denials are documented with Legal.

steps.label: Confirm return date and reinstatement
steps.detail: Two weeks before return, manager and HRBP confirm the same or an equivalent (US) or comparable (Canada) role, pay and grade, any fitness-for-duty certificate announced in the designation notice, and lactation or phased-return needs.
steps.control: Reinstatement equivalence checked by HRBP.

steps.label: Close leave and restore pay
steps.detail: Payroll ends the leave status, restarts salary and deductions, recovers premium arrears within policy caps, stops SUB and top-up payments and reconciles statutory offsets.

steps.label: Employee returns to work
steps.detail: Employee is active in Darwinbox and the return plan passes to LV-03.

controls.control: Eligibility, rights and designation notices issued within 5 business days
controls.evidence: Vendor SLA report and Darwinbox notice log reviewed monthly

controls.control: Certifications stored only in the vendor system or restricted Darwinbox folder; managers see dates and status only
controls.evidence: Role-based access configuration and quarterly access review

controls.control: Every leave-related pay change (paid/unpaid, top-up, statutory offset) reviewed by a second payroll analyst before close
Termination, demotion, PIP or RIF selection of an employee on, or recently back from, protected leave requires Legal review
controls.evidence: Legal sign-off in the case record

controls.control: Protected-period flags block termination transactions in Darwinbox for China (pregnancy, maternity, nursing, medical treatment period) and Taiwan (maternity leave, occupational injury treatment)
controls.evidence: Darwinbox workflow rule and exception log

controls.control: Canadian ROE filed within 5 calendar days after the pay period with an interruption of earnings, and SUB plan registered before top-ups are paid
controls.evidence: ROE submission log and Service Canada SUB registration

kpis.name: Notice timeliness
kpis.why: Late notices weaken the employer's ability to count leave and invite interference claims.

kpis.name: Request-to-designation time
kpis.why: Employees plan pay and care around the decision.

kpis.name: Leave pay accuracy
kpis.target: >= 99.5% of leave pay periods without correction
kpis.why: Overpayments are hard to recover from people on leave; underpayments hurt trust.

kpis.name: Retention 12 months after parental leave
kpis.why: Shows whether return planning and flexibility work.

kpis.name: Leave-related retaliation or interference findings
kpis.why: The core legal risk of the process.

considerations: One front door, two engines: the US vendor handles the multi-state PFML and sick-leave matrix and the leave team runs non-US rules in Darwinbox, but employees and managers see one policy (POL-35), one intake and one status page.

California stacking is the biggest planning item: PDL (up to 4 months) and CFRA bonding (12 weeks) do not run concurrently, so a birthing parent can have about 7 months of job protection, while PFL and SDI replace wages but give no job protection of their own.

Design company paid parental leave as a top-up that integrates with SDI/PFL, EI (through a registered SUB plan), ESI and Taiwan/China statutory allowances; paying full salary on top of statutory benefits creates overpayments and, in Canada, EI clawbacks.

Engineers on tape-out or customer-escalation schedules often want intermittent or partial leave; configure Darwinbox for hours (Taiwan family care leave hourly up to 56 hours) and single days (Taiwan parental leave up to 30 days per parent from 2026) instead of forcing full-day or full-week blocks.

Medical confidentiality is non-negotiable: Taiwan's PDPA and China's PIPL treat health data as sensitive (separate consent, and a PIPIA before transfer to US systems), and India needs consent under the SPDI Rules now and DPDP from 13 May 2027.

Keep equity vesting running through statutory leaves; any tolling for non-statutory personal leave must be in the plan, communicated at grant and checked locally, because Canadian courts read forfeiture terms strictly (Matthews v. Ocean Nutrition).
Never let leave exhaustion auto-terminate anyone: route to accommodation review (ADA/FEHA, Canadian duty to accommodate), and in China remember the medical treatment period bars Art. 40 termination.

RIFs and reorganizations that touch people on leave need decisions made on legitimate criteria, ideally before the leave began, and selection must not count protected absence against performance (Taiwan bars adverse appraisal for up to 10 sick days a year from 2026).

Update the Shanghai handbook through democratic procedure: sick pay there now follows contract or handbook terms after the 1995/2000 notices lapsed on 15 Aug 2026, with a floor of 80% of minimum wage.

variations.how: PDL covers the disability period (up to 4 months), then CFRA gives 12 weeks of bonding; SDI then PFL (up to 8 weeks) replace 70-90% of wages (max $1,765/week in 2026), company paid leave tops up, and FMLA runs alongside where eligible.
No certification is needed to start; reemployment rights cover up to 5 cumulative years, health continuation up to 24 months, and 401(k) make-up contributions are due on return.

Workers' comp governs wage replacement and FMLA/CFRA is designated concurrently where eligible; Taiwan work-injury leave is on full pay (LSA Art. 59) and China's work-injury rules apply during the stoppage period.
Track in hours in Timekeeping; exempt US salary may be reduced for unpaid intermittent FMLA hours without losing the exemption; recertify at reasonable intervals.

variations.when: Employee on H-1B or another work visa
variations.how: Coordinate with Immigration before unpaid leave or schedule changes so wage and status obligations are checked (MV-06).

Ontario long-term illness leave (27 weeks after 13 weeks' employment, practitioner certificate) or BC serious personal illness or injury leave (27 weeks); coordinate STD/LTD and EI sickness benefits and continue benefits.
Apply 158 days (Shanghai) or 178 days (Guangdong) plus paternity leave (10/15 days) and childcare leave (5/10 days a year until age 3); claim maternity allowance and top up to salary where required.

countries.us: FMLA (50+ employees within 75 miles; 12 months and 1,250 hours) gives 12 weeks (26 for military caregivers) of job-protected leave with group health continued; notices are due within 5 business days and certification within 15 calendar days. Layer state PFML (MN and DE benefits from Jan 1, 2026, ME from May 1, 2026; WA job protection at 25+ employees from 2026) and state sick-leave laws by work location. USERRA protects up to 5 cumulative years of service with up to 24 months of health continuation, and ADA leave beyond FMLA can be a reasonable accommodation.
countries.us-ca: CFRA (5+ employees; 12 months and 1,250 hours) gives 12 weeks, including care for grandparents, siblings, adult children and a designated person, and PDL gives up to 4 months per pregnancy separate from CFRA. EDD pays SDI for up to 52 weeks and PFL for up to 8 weeks at 70-90% of wages (max $1,765/week in 2026), and employers cannot require vacation to be used first (AB 2123). Bereavement leave is 5 days within 3 months and reproductive loss leave 5 days per event (max 20 days in 12 months), both after 30 days' service.
countries.ca: Ontario ESA: pregnancy 17 weeks, parental up to 61/63 weeks, family caregiver 8 weeks, critical illness 17/37 weeks, family medical 28 weeks and long-term illness 27 weeks (since June 19, 2025). BC: compassionate care 27 weeks, critical illness 16/36 weeks and serious personal illness or injury 27 weeks (since Nov 28, 2025). EI pays 55% up to about C$729/week (2026) for 35 standard weeks or 33% over 61 extended weeks; top-ups need a registered SUB plan, and benefits and seniority continue during leave with reinstatement to the same or a comparable job.
countries.in: Under SS Code Ch. VI, maternity leave is 26 weeks (no more than 8 before delivery) for the first two children, 12 weeks from the third child, 12 weeks for adoption of a child under 3 months or a commissioning mother, 6 weeks for miscarriage and 1 extra month for related illness, after 80 days worked in the prior 12 months. Pay is the average daily wage, and ESI pays maternity and sickness benefits for employees earning up to INR 21,000/month. There is no statutory paternity leave, and nursing breaks continue until the child is 15 months.
countries.tw: Maternity leave is 8 weeks (full pay after 6 months' service, half pay before), with 7 days each of paid prenatal check-up and paternity leave. Unpaid parental leave runs up to 2 years per child under 3 with an Employment Insurance allowance totalling 80% for up to 6 months per parent, and from 2026 up to 30 days per parent can be taken in single days on 5 days' notice. Family care leave (7 days a year) can be taken hourly up to 56 hours, and termination is barred during maternity leave and occupational-injury treatment.
countries.cn: National maternity leave is 98 days (15 prenatal; +15 for a difficult birth; +15 per additional baby); Shanghai totals 158 days with 10 days' paternity and 5 days a year of childcare leave to age 3, and Guangdong/Shenzhen 178 days with 15 days' paternity and 10 days a year of childcare leave. Maternity allowance comes from maternity insurance, with employer top-up where it is below salary. Medical treatment periods of 3-24 months are protected; Shanghai sick pay now follows contract or handbook terms (floor 80% of minimum wage) and Shenzhen requires at least 60% of normal wage.

processes.name: Workplace accommodation
processes.summary: Handles requests for workplace adjustments linked to disability, pregnancy and related conditions, lactation or religion, from candidates and employees, through a documented and confidential interactive process. Covers ADA, PWFA, FEHA and Title VII religious accommodation (Groff), Canada's duty to accommodate to undue hardship and AODA, India's RPwD Act, Taiwan's maternal-health and disability rules and China's female-employee protections, including lab and cleanroom situations. Good looks like: acknowledgement within 2 business days, decisions within 10 business days, effective accommodations delivered promptly, and medical information kept separate.
processes.owner: Benefits - Leave & Accommodation team (process), HRBP (interactive process), Legal (denials and undue hardship), EHS (lab and reproductive-hazard assessments)
processes.trigger: Any request or expressed need for a change at work linked to a medical condition, pregnancy, lactation, disability or religious practice (a verbal request is enough), or HR/manager awareness of an obvious need
outputs: Confidential accommodation case using T-ACCOMMODATION
Medical information limited to functional limitations, in a restricted file
Interactive process notes with options considered
Written decision with effective and review dates
Fulfilment tickets (equipment, workspace, schedule, access)
AODA individual accommodation plan (Ontario)
processes.sla: Acknowledge within 2 business days; decision within 10 business days of complete information; standard equipment delivered within 10 business days

steps.label: Request accommodation in any form
steps.detail: Employee (or a candidate through the recruiter) asks for an adjustment in any words or channel, and managers who hear a request or see an obvious need route it to the Leave & Accommodation team within 1 business day. The T-ACCOMMODATION form helps but is never a precondition.

steps.label: Acknowledge and open confidential case
steps.detail: The case manager acknowledges within 2 business days, opens a restricted case outside the personnel file, explains confidentiality and next steps, and puts any urgent interim measure in place (seating, breaks, a remote day).
steps.control: Case opened in the restricted repository.

steps.label: Medical documentation needed?
steps.detail: Documentation is requested only when the limitation or need is not obvious; pregnancy needs covered by PWFA, lactation and religious requests normally go straight to the interactive meeting.

steps.label: Request limited medical information
steps.detail: Ask the provider only about functional limitations, expected duration and suggested adjustments, not the diagnosis. Ontario and BC sick-note limits apply to short absences, not to information reasonably needed to accommodate.

steps.label: Provide provider information
steps.detail: Employee returns the provider questionnaire within 15 business days; the case manager follows up rather than closing silently, and delays do not stop interim measures.

steps.label: Hold interactive process meeting
steps.detail: HRBP and the case manager meet the employee to understand limitations, essential functions and options, then consult the manager on operational facts without sharing medical details. Every option considered and the reason for each outcome goes into T-ACCOMMODATION.

steps.label: Lab, cleanroom or hazard involved?
steps.detail: EHS screens whether the role involves chemicals, gases, lasers, X-ray, high voltage, cleanroom gowning or other exposures relevant to the request.

steps.label: Assess hazards and safe alternatives
steps.detail: EHS reviews the job hazard analysis: reproductive hazards (certain glycol ethers, lead, solvents), heat under cleanroom gowning, religious head coverings and beard covers with gowning, lasers and ESD footwear with orthotics. Offer informed choices and reassignment options; never impose a blanket 'fetal protection' exclusion.

steps.label: Evaluate options with HR
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP test options against essential functions and business needs: schedule changes, remote days, equipment, task swaps, temporary suspension of an essential function (PWFA), leave (LV-01), or reassignment to a vacant role as a last resort.

steps.label: Effective option without undue hardship?
steps.detail: The case manager confirms whether the requested or an equally effective option can be provided.

steps.label: Review proposed denial or alternative
steps.detail: Legal reviews any denial or any alternative different from the request against the applicable standard: ADA/FEHA undue hardship, 'substantial increased costs' under Groff v. DeJoy for religion, and Canada's high undue-hardship bar (cost, health and safety). The analysis is written before the decision issues.
steps.control: No denial without Legal sign-off.

steps.label: Issue written decision
steps.detail: The case manager sends the decision with the accommodation, start date, responsibilities, review date and how to ask for changes; denials give reasons and the alternatives offered. Ontario records an individual accommodation plan.

steps.label: Implement workspace and equipment
steps.detail: Facilities and IT fulfil tickets (ergonomic equipment, assistive software, accessible parking, lactation room access, quiet space, prayer room booking); People Ops updates schedules or remote status in Darwinbox and Timekeeping.

steps.label: Apply accommodation and protect employee
steps.detail: Manager implements schedule and task changes, adjusts goals fairly and keeps the reason confidential from the team. Any adverse action within 6 months of the request goes through Employee Relations review.

steps.label: Monitor and review
steps.detail: Check effectiveness at 30 days, then at the review date or when circumstances change (pregnancy stage, return from leave, new role); temporary PWFA measures end on schedule with notice.

steps.label: Accommodation in place and recorded
steps.detail: The case closes with outcome and dates recorded; medical records stay in the restricted file under POL-49 retention.

raci.activity: Route request and open confidential case
Undue hardship, denial or alternative decision
Schedule and remote-status changes in systems

controls.control: Accommodation and medical records kept in a restricted repository separate from personnel files (ADA, CMIA, PDPA, PIPL)
controls.evidence: Access control list and quarterly access review

controls.control: Acknowledgement within 2 business days and decision within 10 business days of complete information
Any denial, or an alternative different from the request, reviewed and signed off by Legal
controls.evidence: Written undue-hardship analysis in the case file

controls.control: Pregnancy and reproductive-hazard decisions made case by case with an EHS assessment; no blanket exclusions
Adverse actions within 6 months after a request routed to Employee Relations
Ontario individual accommodation plans documented (AODA IASR, 50+ employees)

kpis.name: Acknowledgement within 2 business days
kpis.why: Delay is the most common failure-to-engage allegation.

kpis.name: Request-to-decision time
kpis.why: Shows whether the interactive process keeps moving.

kpis.name: Effective accommodation rate
kpis.target: >= 90% resolved with the requested or an effective alternative
kpis.why: Shows the process solves problems rather than filtering requests.

kpis.name: Equipment fulfilment time
kpis.why: An approved but undelivered accommodation is still a failure.

kpis.name: Accommodation-related charges or complaints
kpis.why: Primary legal risk indicator.

considerations: Train managers that any expression of need is a request ('since my surgery I can't stand at the bench all day'); the clock starts then, not when a form arrives.

PWFA: do not demand documentation when the need is obvious, and consider temporary suspension of an essential function. The EEOC rule's elective-abortion provisions were vacated (W.D. La., May 21, 2025) and the EEOC's 2026 agenda targets narrowing 'related medical conditions', so apply the current rule until it changes; California FEHA and PDL are broader anyway.

Religious requests after Groff v. DeJoy (2023) can be refused only for 'substantial increased costs'; typical semiconductor cases are tape-out or on-call schedules on holy days, prayer breaks during long lab sessions, and head coverings or beards under cleanroom gowning.
Judge remote work as an accommodation on essential functions, not general return-to-office policy: validation and failure-analysis roles need the lab, while RTL design and verification often do not.
Bring EHS in early on lab and cleanroom cases: reproductive-hazard exposure, heat stress in gowning and ESD requirements have safe alternatives more often than managers assume.
Mental-health requests are rising: offer flexible hours, quiet space, EAP and clear written priorities, and never apply '100% healed' return rules.
Automated assessments in hiring (coding tests, video tools) must offer an alternative on request; California's CRD ADS rules make this an accommodation duty (TA-03).
Keep diagnoses out of Darwinbox, email and chat: managers get the adjustment and the review date, nothing more.

Feed accommodation data (with consent) into Taiwan's disability quota tracking (67+ employees, 1%) and India's RPwD equal opportunity policy so hiring and retention of people with disabilities is visible.

variations.how: US: PWFA/PDL adjustments and PUMP Act breaks; California: private non-bathroom lactation space with surface, seating, electricity, sink and refrigerator access; Taiwan: maternal health assessment and no night work 10pm-6am; China: no extended hours or night work from 7 months and a 1-hour nursing break until age 1; India: nursing breaks until 15 months.
No medical documentation; consider shift swaps, floating holidays, prayer space and dress adjustments compatible with gowning, and send any refusal to Legal under the Groff standard.

Recruiter routes the request from Greenhouse to the case manager; offer alternative interview formats or extra assessment time, and state the availability of accommodation in Ontario recruitment (AODA).
Finite additional leave after FMLA or ESA entitlements run out is decided here and administered through LV-01.
Coordinate modified duty with workers' comp restrictions (LV-04) and the return plan (LV-03).
Decide the accommodation here first, then MV-04 handles tax, payroll and export-control consequences of the work location.

countries.us: The ADA and PWFA (15+ employees) require an interactive process; under PWFA, avoid documentation when the need is obvious and consider leave, telework and temporary suspension of essential functions. The PWFA rule's elective-abortion provisions were vacated on May 21, 2025 and the EEOC plans an NPRM narrowing 'related medical conditions', so apply the current regulations until amended. Religious accommodation under Title VII uses the Groff v. DeJoy 'substantial increased costs' standard, and the PUMP Act gives lactation breaks and a private non-bathroom space for 1 year after birth.
countries.us-ca: FEHA (5+ employees) makes failure to engage in a timely, good-faith interactive process a separate violation, and the written procedure must cover disability, pregnancy and religion, including requests arising from AI or automated assessments. PDL includes reasonable accommodation and transfer. Labor Code 1030-1034 requires a lactation policy and a private non-bathroom space near the work area with a surface, seating, electricity, and access to a sink and refrigerator.
countries.ca: The Ontario and BC Human Rights Codes require accommodation on protected grounds (disability, family status, creed and others) to the point of undue hardship, judged on cost and health and safety, and the employer must show a genuine search for options as well as the result. AODA requires documented individual accommodation plans and a return-to-work process (50+ employees), individualized workplace emergency response information and notice of accommodation in recruitment. Ontario cannot require a medical note for the 3 ESA sick days but may ask for information reasonably needed to accommodate.
countries.in: The RPwD Act 2016 s.21 requires every establishment to publish an equal opportunity policy (preferably on its website) and provide reasonable accommodation, and private establishments with 20+ employees appoint a liaison officer (verify against the current RPwD Rules). ESI eligibility extends to INR 25,000/month for persons with disability, and maternity-related accommodations include nursing breaks to 15 months and WFH by agreement. Health information needs consent under the SPDI Rules now and DPDP from 13 May 2027.
countries.tw: Employers with 67+ employees must employ persons with disabilities equal to at least 1% of headcount or pay the shortfall into the disability employment fund (People with Disabilities Rights Protection Act Art. 38, 43). OSH Act Art. 30-31 requires risk assessment and job adjustment for pregnant and post-partum (1 year) workers, with a written program at 100+ workers and hazardous sites, and pregnant or breastfeeding employees may not work nights (10pm-6am).
