Health data is sensitive under the PDPA and needs a statutory basis or written consent.
countries.cn: The Employment Promotion Law bars disability discrimination, and the Special Provisions on Labor Protection of Female Employees bar extended hours and night work from 7 months of pregnancy, count prenatal visits as working time, give a 1-hour daily nursing break until the child turns 1 and prohibit listed exposures for pregnant and nursing staff. Disability employment quotas and the related fund levy are set locally (verify Shanghai and Shenzhen ratios). Medical information is sensitive PI under PIPL, needing separate consent and a PIPIA before any transfer to US systems.

processes.name: Return to work
processes.summary: Brings employees back from medical, parental, military or injury leave to the same or an equivalent role, with pay, access and benefits working on day one. Covers fitness-for-duty documentation, reinstatement checks, phased returns and accommodations, and fair treatment in performance and pay cycles. Good looks like: systems and pay working on the first day, a planned first 30 days, and high retention a year later.
processes.owner: Benefits - Leave & Accommodation team (process), HRBP (reinstatement), Manager (reboarding)
processes.trigger: Scheduled leave end 10 business days away, an early-return request, or a provider release to work
outputs: Confirmed return date and reinstatement record (role, grade, pay, location)
Fitness-for-duty or restriction note where required
Reactivated Darwinbox status, system access and badge
Restarted pay and deductions with arrears plan
Phased return or accommodation plan
30-day check-in note
processes.sla: Return confirmed 10 business days ahead; systems active on the return day; 30-day check-in

steps.label: Confirm return date
steps.detail: The case manager confirms the return date with the employee 10 business days ahead, checks for any extension request and alerts the manager and People Ops.

steps.label: Fitness or restriction note needed?
steps.detail: Only if the designation notice announced it (FMLA) or the uniform policy for that condition or job requires it, for example lab or safety-sensitive roles.

steps.label: Provide fitness-for-duty note
steps.detail: Employee provides a provider release listing any restrictions; the case manager reviews it and shares only the restrictions with the manager.

steps.label: Prepare reinstatement and reboarding
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP confirm the same or an equivalent role, pay, grade and reporting line; if the role changed during leave (reorganization, new manager) the reason is documented and Legal reviews it. Build a 2-week reboarding plan covering project context, tool changes and lab re-certification.
steps.control: HRBP compares pre-leave and return records.

steps.label: Reactivate status and access
steps.detail: People Ops ends the leave status in Darwinbox from the return date, restores accounts, badge and lab access through ITSM, and assigns any mandatory training that lapsed during leave.

steps.label: Restart pay and deductions
steps.detail: Payroll restarts salary and benefit deductions, sets up premium arrears recovery within policy caps, ends top-up or SUB payments and records the return in Timekeeping.

steps.label: Phased return or accommodation?
steps.detail: Triggered by restrictions, an employee request or the nature of the absence (long illness, injury).

steps.label: Agree phased or modified plan
steps.detail: The case manager agrees a phased schedule or modified duties with end dates through LV-02 and T-ACCOMMODATION; Ontario employers with 50+ employees document the AODA return-to-work process.

steps.label: Hold 30-day check-in
steps.detail: Manager reviews workload, lactation or care needs and goals, pro-rates objectives for the leave period and confirms the employee is in the current compensation and performance cycle.

steps.label: Fully back at work
steps.detail: The leave case closes; any continuing accommodation stays open in LV-02 with its own review date.

raci.activity: Reinstatement to same or equivalent role

controls.control: Reinstatement equivalence check (role, grade, pay, location) before return; any change needs Legal review
controls.evidence: Return checklist in the case file

controls.control: First-payroll reconciliation of pay, deductions and arrears after return
Fitness-for-duty requests limited to conditions and jobs defined in policy and announced in advance
controls.evidence: Designation notice template and policy matrix

kpis.name: Systems and access ready on return day
kpis.why: Day-one friction tells the employee they were forgotten.

kpis.name: Retention 12 months after return
kpis.why: Main outcome measure of the leave experience.

kpis.name: Post-return payroll corrections
kpis.why: Arrears and deduction errors are common and avoidable.

considerations: Include people on leave in merit, bonus and promotion cycles; pro-rate goals for time away but never mark anyone down for protected leave (Taiwan bars adverse appraisal for up to 10 sick days a year from 2026).
Avoid '100% healed' rules and automatic termination when someone cannot return on the planned date; move to accommodation review first.
Long absences (6+ months) need real reboarding: toolchain and flow changes, project handovers and lab safety re-certification.
Lactation needs are predictable; book the room and agree break times before the first day back.
If the role changed during leave because of a reorganization, document that the decision was made on legitimate grounds unrelated to the leave.

variations.how: Lactation space and breaks, optional phased return, India creche access at 50+ employees, China 1-hour nursing break to age 1, and no night work in Taiwan while breastfeeding.
Modified duty matching workers' comp restrictions (LV-04); check Ontario WSIA re-employment obligations (verify thresholds).
Contact in writing, check for extension or accommodation, then treat as resignation or separation only under local rules and after HRBP and Legal review (OF-01, OF-02).

countries.us: FMLA restores the same or an equivalent position with equivalent pay and benefits; a fitness-for-duty certification may be required only if announced in the designation notice, and ADA return-to-work exams must be job-related.
countries.us-ca: CFRA and PDL give reinstatement to the same or a comparable position (PFL alone does not), and a lactation space meeting Labor Code 1030-1034 must be ready on the return date.
countries.ca: Ontario and BC ESA require reinstatement to the same or a comparable job with seniority credited for the leave, and AODA requires a documented return-to-work process for disability absences at 50+ employees.
countries.in: No dismissal during maternity leave; nursing breaks continue until the child is 15 months, WFH can be agreed where the work allows, and a creche (4 visits a day) is required at 50+ employees.
countries.tw: Reinstate after parental leave and do not treat protected leave adversely (Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 21, 36), and keep pregnant or breastfeeding employees off night work (10pm-6am).
countries.cn: Nursing employees with a child under 1 get a 1-hour daily nursing break and no extended hours or night work, and the employer cannot terminate under LCL Art. 40 or 41 during pregnancy, maternity or nursing periods.

processes.name: Occupational injury & workers' comp claims
processes.summary: Manages work-related injury and illness claims from first report to closure: claim forms, insurer or board filings, wage replacement, medical management, modified duty and return to work. Covers US state workers' comp (California DWC-1 within 1 working day), Ontario WSIB and WorkSafeBC reporting within 3 days, India ESI and employer compensation liability, Taiwan occupational accident insurance and China work-injury recognition within 30 days. Good looks like: every claim filed on time, injured employees paid correctly and back to meaningful work quickly.
processes.owner: Benefits (claims process), EHS (recording and investigation through HS-01), Payroll (wage continuation), carrier or statutory board (adjudication)
processes.trigger: Employee reports a work-related injury or illness, or the company learns of one, including remote-work and business-travel injuries
outputs: Claim form given to the employee (e.g., DWC-1) and employer report to carrier or board
OSHA 300/301 or local register entry through HS-01
Claim number, compensability decision and benefit schedule
Modified-duty offer and return-to-work plan
Wage continuation and statutory offset records
Claim closure and reserve review
processes.sla: Claim form within 1 working day (California); board report within 3 days (Ontario, BC); China recognition application within 30 days

steps.label: Report injury or illness
steps.detail: Employee reports to the manager or EHS immediately or by the end of the shift, including remote-work and business-travel injuries; late reports are still accepted and never penalized.

steps.label: Arrange care and notify
steps.detail: Manager gets first aid or medical care (emergency services first), then notifies EHS and Benefits the same day through the incident form. Managers do not decide whether an injury is work-related.

steps.label: Give claim form and file report
steps.detail: California: give the DWC-1 within 1 working day and report to the carrier. Ontario: WSIB Form 7 within 3 business days; BC: WorkSafeBC within 3 days. India: ESI accident report for covered staff or notice to the employee compensation insurer; Taiwan: occupational accident insurance claim; China: work-injury recognition application within 30 days.
steps.control: Filing date tracked against the statutory deadline.

steps.label: Record and assess reportability
steps.detail: EHS records the case (OSHA 300/301 within 7 calendar days or the local register) and assesses regulator reporting through HS-01; investigation findings feed prevention, not the claim decision.

steps.label: Adjudicate claim and pay benefits
steps.detail: The carrier or TPA, WSIB, WorkSafeBC, ESIC, Taiwan's Bureau of Labor Insurance or the local social insurance bureau decides compensability and pays medical and wage benefits; Benefits supplies wage data and job descriptions promptly.

steps.label: Lost time or restrictions?
steps.detail: Based on the treating provider's work status report.

steps.label: Coordinate leave and modified duty
steps.detail: Benefits designates FMLA/CFRA concurrently where eligible (LV-01) and offers modified duty matching the restrictions (LV-03). Taiwan work-injury leave is on full pay with termination barred during treatment; China pays original wages during the stoppage-with-pay period (generally up to 12 months; verify).

steps.label: Apply wage continuation and offsets
steps.detail: Payroll applies the company wage-continuation or top-up policy net of statutory benefits (for example Taiwan employer liability offset by occupational accident insurance under LSA Art. 59), avoiding double pay and keeping benefit deductions running.

steps.label: Close claim and confirm full duty
steps.detail: Benefits confirms full duty or permanent restrictions, closes the claim with the carrier or board, reviews reserves with the broker and passes lessons to EHS.

steps.label: Back at work, claim closed
steps.detail: Employee is at full or permanently adjusted duty and the claim file is closed and retained.

raci.activity: Claim forms and carrier or board filings
Modified duty and return to work

controls.control: Statutory filing deadlines tracked for each claim (DWC-1 1 working day, WSIB Form 7 3 business days, WorkSafeBC 3 days, China 30 days)
controls.evidence: Claims log with notice and filing dates

controls.control: No discipline, incentive loss or testing practice that deters injury reporting (29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1)(iv))
controls.evidence: Employee Relations review of actions within 90 days of a claim; annual incentive program review

controls.control: Wage continuation reconciled to statutory benefits each pay period to prevent double payment

kpis.name: Claims filed within statutory deadline
kpis.why: Late filing shifts costs to the employer (China) and draws penalties.

kpis.name: Lost-time claims offered modified duty within 5 business days
kpis.why: Early return shortens claims and improves recovery.

kpis.name: Median lost days per lost-time claim
kpis.why: Measures both safety and claim management.

considerations: Home-office injuries in the course of work are compensable, so buy coverage in every state where an employee works (monopolistic state funds in ND, OH, WA and WY).
For travel to foundry and OSAT sites in Taiwan and China, confirm home-country workers' comp covers work abroad and add travel medical and assistance so claims are not stranded in the host country.
In India only staff at or below INR 21,000/month are in ESI; everyone else is covered by employer liability under SS Code Ch. VII, so buy employee compensation or group personal accident insurance.
In China a sudden death at work or within 48 hours of onset counts as work injury, and late recognition applications leave the employer paying benefits for the delay.
Keep medical details in the claim file only; managers get restrictions and dates.

variations.when: Occupational disease (lab chemical exposure, repetitive strain)
variations.how: Longer latency; the China 30-day window runs from diagnosis, and exposed China staff need exit health exams before separation.
The assistance vendor manages care, the home-country carrier is notified and any host-country reporting runs through HS-02.
Immediate regulator notice through HS-01, family support and OF-09; Legal manages communications and privilege.

countries.us: Workers' comp is state-based (monopolistic funds in ND, OH, WA and WY) and covers remote workers; record work-related cases on the OSHA 300 log within 7 days, keep records 5 years and post the 300A from Feb 1 to Apr 30.
countries.us-ca: Give the DWC-1 claim form within 1 working day of learning of the injury (Labor Code 5401) and report serious injuries, illnesses or deaths to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours.
countries.ca: Ontario: report to WSIB (Form 7) within 3 business days of learning of an injury needing health care beyond first aid or causing lost time. BC: report to WorkSafeBC within 3 days, investigate and keep first-aid records.
countries.in: ESI covers employees earning up to INR 21,000/month; for others the employer is liable for compensation under SS Code Ch. VII, and fatal or serious accidents must be reported to the inspector within the rule timelines with an accident register kept.
countries.tw: No-fault employer liability for medical costs and wage replacement (LSA Art. 59) is offset by employer-paid occupational accident insurance benefits; work-injury leave is on full pay and termination is barred during treatment.
countries.cn: Apply for work-injury recognition within 30 days of the accident or occupational-disease diagnosis (Work-Related Injury Insurance Regulations Arts. 15, 17), with sudden death at work within 48 hours counted as work injury; uninsured employers pay the benefits themselves.

processes.name: PTO & holiday administration
processes.summary: Administers paid time off and public holidays in every country: annual holiday calendars, accrual and entitlement rules in Darwinbox, requests and approvals, vacation pay and holiday premiums, leave-year settlement and payout at exit. Covers California's no-forfeiture rule, flexible PTO design, Canadian vacation pay (4%/6%), India's Labour Code accrual and encashment, Taiwan's seniority-based leave with year-end payout and 16 holidays, and China's 13 holidays and 300% pay for untaken leave. Good looks like: correct balances, statutory minimums actually taken or paid, and no surprises at exit.
processes.owner: People Ops (process and configuration), Total Rewards (policy), Payroll (vacation pay and payouts), Managers (approvals)
processes.trigger: Annual holiday-calendar cycle, each time-off request, leave-year end, and every separation
outputs: Country holiday calendars published before the year starts
Tested accrual and entitlement rules in Darwinbox
Approved requests and accurate balances
Leave-year settlement (Taiwan payout, China 300% pay, India encashment)
Exit payout calculations
Quarterly vacation liability report for Finance
processes.sla: Holiday calendars by Dec 1 (China within 2 weeks of the State Council schedule); requests decided within 2 business days; settlement on the first payroll after leave-year end

steps.label: Publish country holiday calendars
steps.detail: People Ops publishes next year's calendars: US company holidays (10-12 plus floating days), Ontario's 9 and BC's 11 statutory holidays, Karnataka national and festival holidays displayed before the year starts, Taiwan's 16 national holidays with make-up days, and China's 13 statutory days with the State Council's swapped workdays.

steps.label: Configure accrual rules in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Configure and test rules by country and tenure: California vacation vesting with a cap plus separate sick leave; Ontario and BC 2-3 weeks with 4%/6% vacation pay; India 1 day per 20 days worked with 30-day carry-forward; Taiwan 3 to 30 days by seniority; China 5/10/15 days by cumulative service.
steps.control: Configuration changes tested and approved before go-live (PY-01).

steps.label: Request time off
steps.detail: Employee requests time off in Darwinbox. Taiwan employees decide when to take statutory annual leave, and China and Canada entitlements must be scheduled so they are actually taken.

steps.label: Approve request?
steps.detail: Manager decides within 2 business days based on coverage, not on whether leave is 'deserved'.

steps.label: Agree alternative dates
steps.detail: Manager proposes alternative dates with a business reason (tape-out, customer escalation) and records it. Statutory minimums cannot be refused outright and must be taken within Ontario's 10-month or BC's 12-month window.

steps.label: Pay vacation pay and holiday premiums
steps.detail: Payroll pays vacation pay (Canada 4%/6% on most wages, including non-discretionary bonuses), holiday work premiums (BC 1.5x plus an average day's pay, Taiwan double pay, China 300%) and non-exempt holiday rules from Timekeeping.

steps.label: Run leave-year settlement
steps.detail: At leave-year end Taiwan pays out unused statutory leave (or defers one year by agreement) and issues the written annual leave statement; China pays 300% for untaken leave unless the employee waived it in writing; India carries forward up to 30 days and encashes the rest; California carries balances forward under the cap.
steps.control: Settlement reconciled before payroll close.

steps.label: Pay out balances at separation
steps.detail: Final pay includes accrued vacation: California at the final rate with final wages (Labor Code 227.3), Taiwan immediately, China pro-rated with 300% for untaken days, India within the 2-working-day full and final settlement, and Ontario/BC outstanding vacation pay.
steps.control: Final-pay checklist includes a vacation balance sign-off.

steps.label: Balances reconciled and reported
steps.detail: People Ops reconciles balances to payroll and gives Finance the vacation liability each quarter; HR Analytics reports usage by team so low-usage teams get attention.

raci.activity: Vacation pay, premiums and leave-year settlement

controls.control: Accrual and holiday configuration changes tested against country rule sets and approved before go-live
controls.evidence: Test scripts and approval in the change log

controls.control: Leave-year statutory settlement (Taiwan payout, China 300%, India encashment) reconciled before payroll close
controls.evidence: Settlement reconciliation signed by the Payroll lead

controls.control: Final pay reviewed for accrued vacation before release

kpis.name: Statutory minimum leave taken or paid
kpis.why: Unpaid statutory leave is a wage claim.

kpis.name: Exit payout and balance errors
kpis.why: California exit errors trigger waiting-time penalties.

kpis.name: Average PTO days taken
kpis.why: Burnout indicator in tape-out-driven teams.

considerations: Flexible or 'unlimited' PTO works only in the US and only if it is genuinely unlimited, not earned and not capped (McPherson v. EF Intercultural); Canada, India, Taiwan and China still need statutory tracking and vacation pay, so run 'flexible' there as the statutory minimum plus discretionary days.
Combining sick leave and vacation into one PTO bank in California makes the whole bank payable at exit; keep paid sick leave separate if payout cost matters.
Canadian vacation pay on non-discretionary bonuses and commissions is a common underpayment for engineers and sales staff; configure payroll to calculate it automatically.

China annual leave depends on cumulative service with all employers, so collect prior-employment evidence at hire; Taiwan employees choose their timing, so managers can negotiate but not assign dates.
India's Code 'wages' definition affects the leave encashment base; recheck CTC structures where basic pay is below 50% of remuneration.

variations.how: Settle the home-country balance under home law (Taiwan payout, China pro-rata), then start host-country accrual; do not carry balances across entities without legal review.

variations.when: Non-exempt lab or shift staff working holidays
variations.how: Pay premiums or give substitute days by country: BC 1.5x plus an average day's pay, Taiwan double pay, China 300% with no substitution, India double pay or a substitute day.

variations.when: Leave during notice period or RIF
variations.how: Ontario and BC vacation pay accrues during statutory notice; China and Taiwan pay out untaken leave at separation; California pays out on the last day.

countries.us: There is no federal vacation mandate, but CO, IL, MA, MT, NE and other states treat accrued vacation as wages, and about 19 states plus DC and many cities mandate paid sick leave with accrual, carryover and notice rules a single PTO policy must meet.
countries.us-ca: Vacation vests as earned: caps are allowed but forfeiture is not, and accrued vacation is paid at the final rate at separation (Labor Code 227.3); paid sick leave gives at least 40 hours/5 days a year (80-hour cap or front-loading) with no payout.
countries.ca: Ontario gives 2 weeks with 4% vacation pay (3 weeks and 6% after 5 years), taken within 10 months; BC gives 2 weeks (4%) after 12 months and 3 weeks (6%) after 5 years, taken within 12 months. Ontario has 9 and BC 11 statutory holidays, and BC holiday work is paid at 1.5x plus an average day's pay (BC high-tech professionals are exempt from Part 5).
countries.in: OSH Code s.32 gives workers with 180+ days in the year 1 day of leave per 20 days worked, a 30-day carry-forward and uncapped encashment of the excess; Karnataka requires about 10 paid holidays (26 Jan, 1 May, 15 Aug, 2 Oct, 1 Nov plus festival holidays) displayed before the year, and polling days are paid holidays.
countries.tw: Annual leave rises with seniority from 3 days (after 6 months) to 30 days; the employee chooses when to take it, unused days are paid out at year end (or deferred one year by agreement) and on termination, and a written annual statement is mandatory. There are 16 national holidays with make-up days when they fall on a day off, and holiday work is paid double.
countries.cn: Annual leave is 5/10/15 days by cumulative service after 12 months' continuous work, pro-rated for joiners and leavers, and untaken leave not waived in writing is paid at 300%. There are 13 statutory holidays under the State Council schedule, and holiday work is paid at 300% with no time-off substitution.

processes.name: Incident & injury reporting
processes.summary: Captures every workplace incident, injury, near miss and unsafe condition, gets people care, meets regulator reporting deadlines, investigates root causes and drives corrective action. Covers offices, labs, remote work and travel in all six jurisdictions and feeds claims (LV-04) and the EHS program (HS-03). Good looks like: plenty of near-miss reports, on-time regulator notices and corrective actions that are closed and verified.
processes.owner: EHS (process), line managers (scene control and corrective actions), Legal (serious incidents and regulator contact)
processes.trigger: Any injury, illness, near miss, dangerous occurrence, violent incident or hazard observation reported by anyone, including contractors and visitors
outputs: Incident record with classification and timestamps
Regulator notifications where required
Investigation report with root cause
Corrective and preventive actions with owners and dates
OSHA 300/301 and local registers; WVPP violent incident log (California)
processes.sla: Serious incidents triaged within 1 hour; regulator notices within statutory limits (as short as 8 hours); investigation within 10 business days; OSHA 300 entry within 7 days

steps.label: Report incident or near miss
steps.detail: Anyone reports through the manager, the EHS form or the hotline immediately; anonymous hazard reports are accepted and no one is penalized for reporting.

steps.label: Secure scene and arrange care
steps.detail: Manager gets first aid or emergency services, stops unsafe work, isolates equipment (lockout/tagout), preserves the scene for serious events and phones EHS for anything beyond first aid.

steps.label: Classify severity and reportability
steps.detail: EHS classifies the event (first aid, recordable, lost time, serious, dangerous occurrence, violent incident), starts the claim path (LV-04) and checks the site's regulator reporting rules.

steps.label: Regulator-reportable event?
steps.detail: Based on severity and each jurisdiction's criteria (fatality, hospitalization, amputation, critical injury, multiple casualties, dangerous occurrence).

steps.label: Notify regulator within deadline
steps.detail: EHS files the notice: federal OSHA within 8 hours for a fatality or 24 hours for hospitalization, amputation or eye loss; Cal/OSHA within 8 hours; Taiwan labor inspection within 8 hours; Ontario and BC board or ministry reports; India inspector per the rules; China local emergency-management authority (verify timing).
steps.control: Notice time logged against event time.

steps.label: Manage inspection and privilege
steps.detail: Legal coordinates inspector visits, document requests and witness interviews, and directs the investigation of serious incidents under privilege where appropriate.

steps.label: Investigate root cause
steps.detail: EHS leads a proportionate investigation (interviews, photos, equipment and training records, 5-whys) with the manager and, where required, the joint health and safety committee. Violent incidents also go into the California WVPP incident log and to ER-07.

steps.label: Complete corrective actions
steps.detail: Manager owns agreed actions (engineering controls, procedure changes, retraining) with due dates; EHS verifies effectiveness before closure.

steps.label: Record, log and trend
steps.detail: EHS records the case on OSHA 300/301 within 7 days (and local registers), has the 300A certified and posted from Feb 1 to Apr 30, submits ITA data by Mar 2 where covered, and reports leading and lagging indicators to leadership.

steps.label: Incident closed, lessons shared
steps.detail: Closure requires completed and verified actions; a short lessons-learned note goes to similar labs and sites.

controls.control: Serious incidents triaged and reportability decided within 1 hour, with timestamps
OSHA 300 entries within 7 days; 300A certified by a company executive and posted Feb 1-Apr 30
Corrective actions tracked to verified closure, with overdue actions escalated monthly
Incentive programs and post-incident drug testing reviewed so they do not deter reporting

kpis.name: Total recordable incident rate (TRIR)
kpis.target: Below prior year and industry benchmark
kpis.why: Headline safety outcome.

kpis.name: Near-miss to recordable ratio
kpis.why: Many near-miss reports signal a healthy reporting culture.

kpis.name: Corrective actions closed on time
kpis.why: Open actions mean the same incident will recur.

kpis.name: Regulator notices on time
kpis.why: Late notices bring penalties and inspection risk.

considerations: Make reporting easy and blame-free; the fastest safety gains in labs come from near misses (spills, gas alarms, ESD events) that never became injuries.
Keep the safety investigation separate from discipline; if misconduct appears, hand it to Employee Relations (ER-02) under its own process.
Remote-work injuries are recordable if work-related, and incidents at foundry or OSAT sites also sit in the host's system; agree information sharing in advance.
California workplace violence incidents need the WVPP violent incident log and a post-incident investigation, with records kept 5 years.
Contractors, interns and visitors in our labs are covered by this process even when they are not on our payroll.

variations.how: Security and ER-07 lead the threat response; EHS logs the incident and updates the WVPP.

variations.when: Chemical exposure or spill in a lab
variations.how: Spill response under the chemical hygiene plan, exposure monitoring and medical consultation, with US exposure records kept 30 years.

variations.when: Incident during travel or at a customer or foundry site
variations.how: Host-site procedures first, with the travel assistance vendor and HS-02 support; home-country recording and claim follow.

countries.us: Report fatalities within 8 hours and inpatient hospitalization, amputation or eye loss within 24 hours; record cases within 7 days on Forms 300/301, keep them 5 years, post the 300A from Feb 1 to Apr 30 and e-submit by Mar 2 where covered.
countries.us-ca: Report serious injuries, illnesses or deaths to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours (8 CCR 342), and keep the WVPP violent incident log with post-incident investigation and 5-year records.
countries.ca: Ontario: WSIB Form 7 within 3 business days, and critical injuries or deaths need immediate notice to the Ministry, JHSC and any union plus a written report (OHSA s.51; verify timing). BC: report to WorkSafeBC within 3 days, investigate and keep first-aid records.
countries.in: Report fatal and serious accidents to the inspector within the OSH Code rule timelines and keep an accident register; labs that count as 'factories' carry stricter reporting and safety-officer duties.
countries.tw: Report a death, 3+ injured or 1+ hospitalized to the labor inspection agency within 8 hours (OSH Act Art. 37); bullying complaints from 1 July 2026 need case registration in MOL's system.
countries.cn: Report production-safety accidents promptly to the local emergency-management authority (the accident-reporting regulations use a 1-hour rule for the enterprise head; verify) and apply for work-injury recognition within 30 days.

processes.name: Crisis response & duty of care
processes.summary: Protects employees during crises: natural disasters (Taiwan earthquakes and typhoons, California earthquakes and wildfires, Bengaluru flooding), pandemics, civil unrest, violent threats and incidents during travel. Covers detection, crisis team activation, accounting for employees, evacuation and medical support, pay and leave during closures, EAP and after-action review. Good looks like: every affected employee accounted for within hours, clear pay rules, and playbooks that improve after each event.
processes.owner: Security (crisis management and travel risk), HRBP (people support), People Ops (rosters), EHS (site emergency plans)
processes.trigger: Alert from the travel risk vendor, a government warning (e.g., a Taiwan typhoon work-suspension announcement), a site emergency, a pandemic declaration or a credible threat
outputs: Crisis activation log and decisions
Affected-employee roster and accounting status
Evacuation and support actions
Country pay, leave and remote-work instructions
EAP and critical-incident support offered
After-action review and playbook updates
processes.sla: Crisis team convened within 1 hour; 100% of affected employees accounted for within 4 hours; pay instructions before the next payroll close; after-action review within 2 weeks

steps.label: Detect event and alert
steps.detail: Security monitors the travel risk vendor, government alerts (Taiwan CWA typhoon and earthquake warnings, local work-suspension announcements), site alarms and threat reports, and triages severity against the crisis playbook.

steps.label: Activate crisis team?
steps.detail: Activation criteria: people injured or at risk, a site closed, or travellers in an affected area.

steps.label: Pull affected-employee roster
steps.detail: People Ops pulls employees, contractors and interns by work site and home location from Darwinbox, and travellers from the travel booking feed, with emergency contacts.
steps.control: Roster taken from system data, not spreadsheets.

steps.label: Confirm safety via check-in
steps.detail: Employees answer the mass-notification check-in (SMS, app, email) or call the hotline; managers phone anyone who has not responded.

steps.label: Everyone accounted for and safe?
steps.detail: Managers confirm status for each team member on the roster.

steps.label: Escalate search and support
steps.detail: Security escalates to the assistance vendor, local authorities and site leads for evacuation, medical support or search; HRBP contacts next of kin with care, and fatalities move to OF-09.

steps.label: Apply pay, leave and EAP support
steps.detail: HRBP issues country instructions: office closure and remote work, pay during closures (US exempt salary rules, Taiwan typhoon work suspension, China stoppage wage rules), emergency leave, salary advances for displaced employees, and EAP or critical-incident counselling.

steps.label: Debrief and update playbooks
steps.detail: Security runs an after-action review with HR, EHS, IT and site leads within 2 weeks covering roster accuracy, response times and communication gaps, and updates playbooks and drills.

steps.label: Event closed
steps.detail: The event log is closed and metrics go to the crisis steering group.

controls.control: Work location, personal phone and emergency contacts validated in Darwinbox twice a year
International travel booked through the approved travel channel so travellers can be located
Annual crisis exercise and evacuation or earthquake drill at every site
Emergency contact and health-status data collected with notice and consent (PIPL, DPDP, PDPA)

kpis.name: Employees accounted for within 4 hours
kpis.why: Core duty-of-care outcome.

kpis.name: Emergency contact completeness
kpis.why: Accounting fails without reachable contacts.

kpis.name: Trips booked through the approved channel
kpis.why: Untracked travellers cannot be found in a crisis.

kpis.name: Drill completion
kpis.why: Plans that are not practised do not work.

considerations: Set closure pay rules before an event: US exempt staff must receive the full weekly salary for a week in which they worked and the employer closed, and most companies also pay non-exempt staff for short closures to avoid hardship.

Taiwan typhoon days: when the local government announces a work suspension, employees cannot be forced to attend or treated as absent; decide in advance whether the day is paid (most MNCs pay) and how those who must work are compensated (verify MOL natural-disaster guidance).
Hsinchu and the Bay Area are both earthquake zones: include lab gas shut-off, chemical storage and cleanroom evacuation in drills, and keep remote-work kits ready.
China travel carries device and data risk under the Counter-Espionage Law and Data Security Law; brief travellers on device handling and cross-border data before customer-fab visits.
Pandemic playbooks should pre-define remote-work triggers, sick-leave extensions and minimal, consent-based health-data collection.

variations.how: Close the site, move to remote work, account for everyone, pay under closure rules and offer emergency advances and EAP; Taiwan follows government work-suspension announcements.
The assistance vendor locates and evacuates, home-country workers' comp or travel medical pays for care, and HRBP supports the family.
Activate remote work, adjust sick leave, use the accommodation process for high-risk employees and limit health-data collection.
Security and ER-07 lead; California employees may leave under Labor Code 1139, and the WVPP incident log is updated.

countries.us: Exempt employees must receive the full weekly salary for any week in which they worked and the employer closed, and sites with more than 10 employees need a written emergency action plan (29 CFR 1910.38).
countries.us-ca: Employees may refuse to report to, or may leave, a workplace during an emergency condition if they reasonably believe it is unsafe and cannot be barred from using phones to seek help (Labor Code 1139); the WVPP covers active threats.
countries.ca: Workers may refuse unsafe work under the Ontario OHSA and BC regulations, AODA requires individualized workplace emergency response information for employees with disabilities, and BC requires working-alone procedures.
countries.in: Night-shift employees need safe transport, well-lit premises and displayed emergency contacts (keep cab security despite Karnataka's 2026 deregulation), and Bengaluru monsoon flooding should trigger remote-work instructions.
countries.tw: When the local government announces a typhoon or disaster work suspension, employees cannot be compelled to work or penalized for absence (verify MOL guidance on pay), and workers may withdraw from imminent danger without adverse treatment (OSH Act Art. 18; verify).
countries.cn: Brief travellers on device handling and cross-border data under the Counter-Espionage Law (2023) and Data Security Law; for work stoppages not caused by employees, pay normal wages for the first pay cycle, then at least minimum wage if work is provided or a local living allowance (Interim Provisions on Wage Payment Art. 12; verify local rates).

processes.name: Lab & EHS safety program
processes.summary: Runs the EHS management system for offices and hardware labs (validation, characterization, reliability, failure analysis, RF and photonics): hazard inventory, written programs, role-based training gates for lab access, inspections, safety committees, health surveillance and an annual review. Covers ESD, lasers, X-ray, high voltage, chemicals and HazCom, reproductive hazards, California IIPP and WVPP, Taiwan occupational health services, and Ontario/BC joint health and safety committees. Good looks like: nobody enters a lab untrained, inspection findings close on time, and customer RBA and ISO 45001 audits pass.
processes.owner: EHS (program), lab managers (daily compliance), Security (lab access), Facilities (engineering controls)
processes.trigger: Annual EHS cycle, a new lab, equipment or chemical, a hire or transfer into a lab role, a regulatory change or an incident finding
outputs: Site hazard and chemical inventory
Written programs (IIPP, WVPP, Chemical Hygiene Plan, HazCom/WHMIS, laser, ESD, emergency action)
Job hazard analyses and PPE assessments
Training records that gate lab access
Inspection and committee minutes with corrective actions
Health examination records and annual management review
processes.sla: Training before lab access; monthly lab inspections; findings closed within 30 days; annual program review

steps.label: Maintain hazard and chemical inventory
steps.detail: EHS keeps the site inventory of chemicals (decapsulation acids, solvents), compressed and toxic gases, lasers by class, X-ray sources, high-voltage benches, thermal chambers and cleanroom areas; any new item gets a pre-use hazard review.

steps.label: Maintain written programs
steps.detail: Keep current: IIPP and WVPP (California), Chemical Hygiene Plan and HazCom (updated for HazCom 2024), WHMIS (Canada), laser safety (ANSI Z136), radiation registrations, ESD (ANSI/ESD S20.20), emergency action and fire plans, the Taiwan OSH plan and the China safety responsibility system.

steps.label: Complete job hazard analysis
steps.detail: The lab manager completes a job hazard analysis and PPE assessment for each lab role, defines required training and flags reproductive-hazard exposures for informed notices.

steps.label: Complete role-based safety training
steps.detail: Employee completes LMS modules (general safety, HazCom/WHMIS, lab-specific, laser or X-ray where relevant) and a practical sign-off; Taiwan new hires get general OSH training (typically 3+ hours) and Ontario workers basic awareness training.
steps.control: Completion and practical sign-off recorded in the LMS.

steps.label: Training and sign-off complete?
steps.detail: The badge system checks the LMS feed for the role's required training.

steps.label: Grant lab badge access
steps.detail: Security grants lab access by role only after the LMS confirms completion, and access expires automatically when refreshers lapse or the employee transfers out.

steps.label: Inspect labs and run committees
steps.detail: EHS and lab managers inspect monthly; the Ontario JHSC and BC JOHSC (20+ workers) meet and inspect on their statutory cadence, and Taiwan occupational health services run to headcount thresholds.

steps.label: Correct hazards and maintain controls
steps.detail: Facilities fixes findings and maintains fume hoods, gas detection, eyewash stations and showers, grounding and interlocks, keeping certification records.

steps.label: Run annual review and health checks
steps.detail: Annual management review of metrics, audits and legal changes aligned to ISO 45001, plus health examinations under local rules (Taiwan periodic exams, China pre-, on- and exit-job exams for exposed staff, India check-ups where prescribed).

steps.label: Program reviewed for the year
steps.detail: The signed annual review, updated programs and next year's objectives are filed and shared with leadership, and with customers on request (RBA).

controls.control: Lab badge access blocked until LMS training and practical sign-off are complete
Annual review and sign-off of the IIPP, WVPP, Chemical Hygiene Plan and HazCom program
Monthly lab inspections with corrective actions tracked to closure
controls.evidence: Inspection checklists and corrective action log

controls.control: Health examinations completed on schedule for exposed staff, and China exit exams completed before separation

kpis.name: Lab access holders with complete training
kpis.why: Untrained access is behind most lab injuries.

kpis.name: Inspection findings closed within 30 days
kpis.why: Measures hazard-correction discipline.

kpis.name: Lost-time lab injuries
kpis.why: Outcome measure for the lab program.

kpis.name: Committee meetings held on statutory cadence
kpis.why: Legal requirement in Ontario, BC and Taiwan.

considerations: Fabless does not mean hazard-free: decapsulation, solvents, compressed gases, lasers, X-ray inspection, thermal chambers and high-voltage benches are real risks, and engineers often work alone late during bring-up, so add working-alone rules.
Reproductive hazards need informed, non-discriminatory handling: notices, exposure assessment and voluntary reassignment options, never pregnancy-based exclusion (LV-02).
Cleanroom gowning counts as clothing that restricts heat removal under California's indoor heat standard, which then applies from 82°F; check lab temperature plans.
Engineers visiting foundry and OSAT cleanrooms in Taiwan and China must complete host-site training and our travel briefing first.
In India a lab with 20+ workers using power becomes a 'factory' with licensing and safety-officer duties, so plan Bengaluru lab headcount growth with EHS.
Customers increasingly ask for RBA Code and ISO 45001 evidence; an audit-ready program protects design wins.

variations.when: New lab, class 3B/4 laser or X-ray equipment
variations.how: Pre-start hazard review, laser safety officer sign-off, state radiation registration and updated training before first use.

variations.when: Pregnant or nursing employee in a lab
variations.how: EHS assessment and LV-02 accommodation, Taiwan maternal health program and China's prohibited-work list, with no forced exclusion.
Scale down to ergonomics, emergency action, violence and harassment programs and first aid.

variations.when: Work at third-party fabs or customer sites
variations.how: Host-site rules plus our travel safety briefing, with incidents reported in both systems (HS-01).

countries.us: OSHA requires a Chemical Hygiene Plan and Chemical Hygiene Officer for labs, HazCom 2024 updates (verify compliance dates), written emergency action and fire prevention plans above 10 employees, and in practice an ANSI Z136 laser program and state X-ray registration.
countries.us-ca: A written IIPP (8 CCR 3203) with inspections and training and a site-specific WVPP with annual interactive training and an incident log (Labor Code 6401.9) are mandatory; Cal/OSHA must adopt a general-industry workplace violence standard by 31 Dec 2026, and the indoor heat standard applies at 82°F with cleanroom gowning.
countries.ca: Ontario needs a JHSC with certified members at 20+ workers (a representative at 6-19), a written OHS policy reviewed annually and WHMIS training; BC needs a JOHSC at 20+ workers (a representative at 10-19) and a formal OHS program at 50+, or 20+ where there is at least moderate hazard such as a lab.
countries.in: Register under the OSH Code at 10+ workers; validation or test labs with 20+ workers using power (40+ without) are 'factories' needing licensing, a safety officer or committee and hazardous-process controls, and annual health check-ups apply to employees aged 40+ where the rules prescribe them.
countries.tw: Labs and test areas are high-risk under the OSH management rules, so keep an OSH plan and designated management staff (verify committee and dedicated-unit thresholds, e.g., 100+ workers); 50-299 workers need contracted physician/nurse services and 300+ must employ nurses, with written violence-prevention and maternal-health programs at 100+.
countries.cn: The Work Safety Law requires a responsibility system with a safety function or full-time safety staff above 100 employees, and exposed lab or test staff need pre-, on- and exit-job occupational health exams (no termination without the exit exam) plus hazardous-chemical storage and training controls.
